title: Sr. Applied Scientist, AWS Applied AI Solutions - Life Sciences
descriptionHtml:
AWS Applied AI Solutions (AAIS) is building toward a future where every business innovates with Amazon AI teammates. To get there, we build AI solutions that improve human capabilities and transform entire business functions. We create end-to-end products that surprise and delight out-of-the-box, making complex things easy and hard things possible, with no cloud experience required. We start with customers who embrace the future and build bridges to meet the rest where they are. We pursue ambitious opportunities with conviction, and we are looking for builders who share that mindset.

The Team Join the next science revolution at AWS Life Sciences Applied AI Solutions where you'll work alongside world-class scientists to build AI that transforms how therapeutics are discovered, developed, and brought to patients.

We're out to revolutionize how medicines are discovered, developed, and brought to patients powered by a new generation of AI. Our team tackles some of the hardest open problems at the intersection of frontier AI and life sciences. We apply biological foundation models large language models and agentic reasoning systems to life sciences problems then put them into the hands of customers as applications and managed services they can fine-tune tailor and deploy on their own data. The science challenges are deep: how do you design agentic systems that reason correctly over complex biological regulatory and clinical logic? How do you enable customers to tailor foundation models to their proprietary data and get better outputs with less effort? How do you adapt models to reason faithfully in high-stakes scientific and regulatory domains?

Today we're focused on two areas. In clinical trials we're building AI that automates and optimizes regulatory and clinical development workflows. In drug design our products (including Amazon Bio Discovery) accelerate discovery by giving bench scientists AI-guided protein engineering and antibody design capabilities. We combine frontier research with production-scale delivery to put breakthrough science into the hands of customers solving humanity's hardest problems.

We value scientific rigor encourage publication and support conference participation. If you want to do research that ships this is the team.

The Role We are seeking an Applied Scientist to build the models and methods behind our life sciences AI products with a primary focus on clinical trial operations and agentic reasoning. You will design train and evaluate systems that reason over complex clinical and operational logic and ship them into products customers use directly. You will work closely with senior and principal scientists on well-scoped research problems own your results end to end and see your work reach production.

This role combines expertise in LLM reasoning and agentic AI with applied impact in life sciences. You will work on how large language models reason plan and act in complex scientific domains while applying domain knowledge to ensure models produce scientifically valid outputs. The problems span multiple fronts:

• How do you build LLM-based agentic systems that correctly reason over clinical protocols regulatory standards and complex multi-step operational workflows?
• How do you evaluate agent reliability and faithfulness rigorously enough to trust in high-stakes clinical settings?
• How do you develop model customization methods (fine-tuning retrieval augmentation domain adaptation) that let customers get strong results from foundation models on their own data?
You will focus on clinical trial operations (agentic automation structured reasoning evaluation domain adaptation) with opportunities to contribute across drug discovery (protein engineering antibody design) as the portfolio grows. You will own end-to-end scientific solutions from research through production and your work will directly shape the tools that scientists use daily.

Key job responsibilities
• Design train fine-tune and evaluate LLM-based agentic systems that reason over clinical protocols regulatory standards and operational workflows
• Build rigorous evaluation harnesses and benchmarks to measure agent reliability faithfulness and failure modes in high-stakes domains
• Develop model customization methods (fine-tuning RLHF retrieval augmentation domain adaptation) that help customers get better outputs on their own data with less effort
• Contribute to graph-based and causal modeling approaches for clinical trial operations
• Partner with Life Sciences domain experts product and engineering to translate scientific challenges into shipped capabilities
• Own experiments end to end: problem framing implementation evaluation iteration and hand-off to production
• Publish at top-tier venues where the work supports it
• Contribute to drug discovery efforts (protein engineering antibody design) as opportunities arise

A day in the life
• Design and run an experiment to validate a new agentic reasoning or fine-tuning method then ship it as a capability customers can use
• Diagnose why a model is failing on a new class of inputs and implement a fix to unblock a delivery milestone
• Build or extend an evaluation benchmark to measure how faithfully an agent reasons over clinical logic
• Meet with domain experts to scope what the next model release needs to do
• Review results with a senior scientist sharpen the approach and get it over the finish line
• Prototype a new idea that could become the next capability in the product

About the team
Amazon values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn't followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don't let it stop you from applying.

Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world's most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that's why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why flexible work hours and arrangements are part of our culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there's nothing we can't achieve in the cloud.

Here at AWS, it's in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity and AmazeCon conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.

We're continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth's Best Employer. That's why you'll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

title: Software Development Engineer, Platform Engineering and Services (AFT Labor Insights)
descriptionHtml:
Amazon Fulfillment Technologies (AFT) powers the physical engine at the heart of Amazon — magically turning your click of a button into packages at your door. Within AFT, the Labor Insights team builds and operates the platform that tracks on associate labor performance across Amazon's entire global warehouse network. Labor Insights' suite of 18+ services supports ~1 million associates and 70,000+ daily portal users across 9,800+ facilities and 10 business lines — ingesting over 19 billion labor events annually to produce the real-time productivity reports that warehouse managers rely on to run their operations every day. We leverage AWS technologies, stream processing, and AI/ML to build distributed, highly available systems that operate at massive scale.

Are you ready for a challenge? As a Software Development Engineer on the Labor Insights team, you will build the next generation of Amazon's labor management platform — designing systems that ingest billions of labor events from warehouse floor tools and time clock systems, aggregate them through multi-stage pipelines, and serve real-time productivity reports to operations managers across the globe. You will own design and development of distributed systems that refresh reports every 10–15 minutes across 3 global regions while maintaining 99.9% availability. You will contribute to a wide range of projects — from event processing pipelines and aggregation engines to reporting APIs, modern React-based portals, and AI-powered configuration tools. Most excitingly, you will help drive refresh of the existing tool, an AI-first greenfield initiative to rebuild the platform from the ground up using modern stream-based architecture, eliminating a decade of technical debt and delivering near real-time metrics. You will be involved in all aspects of the software development cycle including scoping, design, implementation, testing, and delivery. A commitment to teamwork, hustle, and strong communication skills are absolute requirements. Creating reliable, scalable, and high-performance services requires exceptional technical expertise. If you have that expertise, are customer-centric, and motivated about building systems that operate at global scale, then we want to talk to you!


Key job responsibilities
* Design, develop, and test software components across Labor Insights' ingestion, aggregation, reporting, and configuration layers — handling labor events, time clock punches, employee location tracking, and productivity report generation
* Build new services using AI-assisted development practices, leveraging tools like Amazon Q and Bedrock to achieve high-velocity delivery on greenfield systems
* Design large-scale data processing solutions using DynamoDB, PostgreSQL, S3, SQS/SNS, EventBridge, Lambda, and stream processing frameworks (Cosmos/Flink) optimized for high throughput and low-latency access
* Drive service consolidation and modernization — migrating from legacy infrastructure to Native AWS (NAWS) with full CI/CD pipelines
* Participate in definition of coding standards and apply them in code and design reviews
* Provide estimates for development tasks and negotiate timelines with project leaders
* Mentor junior team members and help them acquire critical skills and best practices
* Document and communicate technical concepts to team members and stakeholders
* Participate in deep technical discussions, where you stand up for your ideas and work with team members to find the best solution for the customer
* Identify technical and project risks and take initiative to mitigate them

A day in the life
Full-cycle ownership. You contribute to all aspects of the software development cycle — from scoping and design through implementation, testing, and delivery of features that provide labor performance visibility to Amazon's global fulfillment operations.

Billions-scale data processing. You build systems that ingest 19+ billion labor events per year from warehouse floor tools, time clock systems, and employee location heartbeats. You design multi-stage aggregation pipelines that process this data into PPR and PPA reports refreshed every 10–15 minutes, served to 70K+ daily users across 9,800+ facilities.

AWS-native architecture. You leverage the full AWS stack — DynamoDB for hot data storage, S3 for historical data, PostgreSQL for aggregated reports, SQS/SNS for event-driven processing, EventBridge and Lambda for serverless job orchestration, and Cosmos/Flink for stream processing. You architect for 99.9% availability across 3 global regions (NA, EU, FE).
AI-first development. You pioneer AI-assisted engineering practices — using Amazon Bedrock, Amazon Q, and AI-powered tools to accelerate greenfield development at 20X traditional velocity. You build intelligent systems like AI-powered configuration assistants, automated intake routing, and GenAI-driven operational tooling.

Modernization at scale. You modernize a 15+ year-old platform serving every fulfillment center worldwide — consolidating 23+ services into a clean microservices architecture, rebuilding the portal experience in React from legacy JSP/jQuery, and transitioning from batch to stream processing, all while maintaining zero-downtime operations.


About the team
About Labor Insights: We build Amazon's global labor management platform — the system of record for measuring associate performance across every fulfillment center, sort center, delivery station, and grocery facility worldwide. Labor Insights tracks how ~1 million associates spend their time, producing the productivity reports (PPR, PPA, attendance, Time Off Task) that operations managers use to make staffing decisions, identify bottlenecks, and ensure customer shipments go out on time.

What Makes This Role Exciting:

* Build FCLM 2.0 from the ground up — a once-in-a-career opportunity to greenfield a platform that runs Amazon's global workforce visibility, using AI-first development to deliver in months what would take years through traditional approaches
* Pioneer stream processing — transition from batch to real-time with sub-minute latencies using Cosmos/Flink, fundamentally changing how Amazon tracks labor performance
* Build a multi-tenant platform (FCLM FLEX) — design a configurable translation layer that recasts PPR and PPA as flexible views on the same underlying data, eliminating duplicate pipelines and enabling third-party teams to create custom labor views without engineering support
* Reimagine the portal experience — rebuild the portal used by 70K+ daily users from legacy JSP/jQuery into a modern React application with accessibility, localization, and scalable access controls
* Expand to new businesses — onboard Amazon Grocery (Fresh, Whole Foods) and other new business lines in 2026+, scaling the platform to new node types and labor models
* Build AI-powered tools — design intelligent systems using Amazon Bedrock for automated configuration management, request intake, and operational copilots that serve 1.5M workers globally
* Massive impact — every feature you build is used by tens of thousands of warehouse managers the same day; Labor Insights’ operations save an estimated $25M+ annually


Our tenets:

* Build for Scale: Design generically to support multiple use cases beyond Labor Insights
* Service Generalization for Multi-Tenancy: Build abstractions that work across all businesses
* No Data Filtering by Default: Accept all incoming data, build flexible views on top

Basic qualifications

- 3+ years of non-internship professional software development experience
- 2+ years of non-internship design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience
- 1+ years of software development engineer or related occupational experience
- 1+ years of designing and developing large-scale, multi-tiered, multi-threaded, embedded or distributed software applications, tools, systems, and services using: C#, C++, Java, or Perl experience
- 1+ years of Object Oriented Design experience
- Bachelor's degree or foreign equivalent in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, or a related field
- Experience programming with at least one software programming language

Preferred qualifications

- 3+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience
- Bachelor's degree in computer science or equivalent

You'll work closely with stakeholders to gather requirements, assess current infrastructure through discovery tooling and application owner interviews, and propose effective migration strategies to AWS — assigning R-strategies (Rehost, Replatform, Refactor, Retire, Retain, Relocate) and designing wave plans that respect dependency groupings, capacity constraints, and regulatory frozen zones. As trusted advisors to our customers, providing guidance on migration best practices, risk mitigation, and innovative solutions, you will be responsible for leading the end-to-end migration assessment process, ensuring adherence to AWS well-architected principles, optimizing wave sequencing, and managing risks throughout the programme lifecycle.

The AWS Professional Services organization is a global team of experts that help customers realize their desired business outcomes when using the AWS Cloud. We work together with customer teams and the AWS Partner Network (APN) to execute enterprise cloud computing initiatives. Our team provides assistance through a collection of offerings which help customers achieve specific outcomes related to enterprise cloud adoption. descriptionHtml:
Amazon Global Logistics (AGL) is seeking an Account Manager for UK and EU markets to build and scale the next generation of logistics solutions – bring your sales skills and data-driven approach to transform how enterprises move inventory globally.

AGL is an integrated, end-to-end, supply chain solution that simplifies the complex global logistics for enterprise customers and Amazon's selling partners. With AGL, businesses can seamlessly transport their inventory from the factory door (in overseas locations such as China and Vietnam) directly to locations in US, UK, EU and JP - all with a click of a button. AGL's aim is to optimize the end-to-end supply chain, allowing customers to focus on what they do best – building unique product offerings that their customers love.

Ideal Candidate Profile: You thrive in ambiguity and can juggle multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment. You possess high levels of creativity, flexibility, and attention to detail. You're deeply data-oriented and know how to translate customer requirements into compelling value propositions. You have a proven track record in pipeline development and sales target achievement.

Key job responsibilities
-Recruit and manage a diverse portfolio of Selling Partners for Amazon Global Logistics suite of supply chain services to meet or exceed sales targets (Sellers launched, volume, revenue, etc.)
-Own sales activities including outreach, sales pipeline management, forecasting, operational troubleshooting, Selling Partner education, etc.
-Identify growth opportunities through solutions-based selling by identifying and understanding Selling Partners' supply chain needs
-Conduct persuasive sales presentations to senior external stakeholder such as Directors and business owners
-Actively prospect for new business opportunities, leveraging market insights and network connections
-Program management responsibilities geared to improve and build upon the Selling Partners experience
-Identify and partner with internal teams ensure seamless seller experience and target achievement


A day in the life
Morning: You join the daily standup, sharing operational updates and learnings from recent seller conversations. You then review your pipeline, prioritising outreach by account tier and revenue potential, and shaping your approach around each prospect's supply chain needs. You also work with partner teams like FBA to align on shared accounts and coordinate joint outreach.

Midday: You pitch 4 to 5 prospective sellers a week on AGL's logistics services, turning supply chain solutions into clear value for senior decision makers. You prepare pipeline metrics for leadership reviews, summarising deal progress, flagging risks, and calling out wins.

Afternoon: You contribute to WBR metric reviews and help align team priorities. You own or support a team initiative, such as improving seller onboarding or internal handoffs. You close the day nurturing seller relationships and supporting new sellers through launch.

About the team
Formed in 2020, the EMEA Sales Team within Amazon Global Logistics works closely with Amazon Selling Partners providing onboarding support, operational insights, and direction for new and existing logistics products & services. Our objective over the next few years is to scale our global supply chain program for Amazon Selling Partners and deliver a logistics experience they love.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree or equivalent
- Experience exceeding sales targets using a consultative, solutions-focused approach or equivalent
- Experience influencing at all levels within an organization, particularly at the executive level
- Experience translating customer needs into business requirements
- Speak, write, and read fluently in German

Preferred qualifications

- Experience in sales or marketing work (like e-commerce, retail technology, SaaS) or equivalent
- Experience with MS Office Suite, CRMs (Salesforce) and other systems
- MBA, or Master's degree

Amazon is an equal opportunities employer. We believe passionately that employing a diverse workforce is central to our success. We make recruiting decisions based on your experience and skills. We value your passion to discover, invent, simplify and build. Protecting your privacy and the security of your data is a longstanding top priority for Amazon. title: EHS Specialist
descriptionHtml:
Join Amazon’s mission to become Earth’s safest place to work! At Amazon, we’ve set the ambitious goal to become the benchmark of safety excellence across all industries in which we operate. As a Workplace Health & Safety Specialist (WHSS), you'll be at the forefront of transforming workplace safety culture at one of the world's most innovative companies. Your expertise and dedication will directly protect employees, ensuring they return home safely to their families every day. You'll facilitate new approaches to safety, combining technology with human-centered solutions to create an environment where safety and productivity thrive together. This isn't just about maintaining safety standards – it's about revolutionizing how we think about and implement workplace safety, making a lasting impact on our people and operations. As your building's designated safety champion, you'll have the unique opportunity to build relationships, influence positive change, and help write the next chapter in Amazon's commitment to becoming Earth's Safest Place to Work.

Core Impact Areas:
Safety Program Excellence & Implementation - Drive comprehensive safety programs through data-driven strategies. Lead daily safety audits, incident investigations, and risk assessments while implementing innovative solutions to prevent injuries. Deliver engaging safety training that resonates with associates and promotes a proactive safety culture. Champion continuous improvement initiatives that enhance workplace safety while maintaining operational efficiency.

Associate Advocacy & Cultural Leadership - Serve as a trusted safety advisor and advocate for associate wellbeing, building strong partnerships across all levels of the organization. Foster a culture where safety is everyone's priority through effective communication, coaching, and positive reinforcement. Develop strong relationships with frontline associates and leadership to drive behavioral changes and ensure safety best practices become natural habits. Transform safety data into compelling narratives that influence positive change and drive engagement in safety initiatives.

Additional Job Elements include:
- Lift up to 49 pounds and frequently push, pull, squat, bend, and reach
- Stand/walk for up to 12 hours during shifts
- Work in an environment where the noise level varies
- Work in an environment that is subject to variable temperatures and weather (delivery stations include outside loading departments)
- Continuously climb and descend stairs (applies to sites with stairs)
- Maintain effective care delivery in emergencies and assist emergency response at the site

Must be available to work flexible shifts including days, nights and/or weekends.

For those that do not have an adult First Aid, CPR, AED certification from the American Heart Association or American Red Cross, must obtain within 3 weeks of start date.

Basic qualifications

- High school or equivalent
- A minimum of 1 year in an Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) related field OR; A Bachelor’s degree in EHS-relevant background OR; 6 months experience performing in a safety-related role within Amazon
- Knowledge of OSHA regulations specifically 29 CFR 1910
- Experience using Microsoft Word and Excel in a professional capacity
- Experience maintaining confidentiality in matter involving security and/or personnel issues in the workplace

Preferred qualifications

- Bachelor’s degree or higher, preferably in a safety related field
- Strong communication, teamwork, analysis, judgment, and customer focus skills
- Experience leading and managing a team, ability to analyze accident data, new processes, and machinery for potential safety concerns, and conduct job hazard and job safety analyses
- Experience in emergency response and currently holds First Aid and CPR certificates
- Experience in workers compensation case management

title: Software Development Engineer II, AWS Compute Optimizer
descriptionHtml:
Do you want to build the large-scale data systems that help millions of AWS customers cut their cloud costs and run more efficiently? Join a team that turns massive streams of infrastructure and usage data into the intelligent recommendations customers rely on every day.

We are the Optimization Data team, the data backbone behind AWS Compute Optimizer and AWS's broader cost optimization products. Our job is to identify customer resources, collect the utilization metrics that describe how they run, and turn that raw telemetry into clean, reliable, well-labeled signals that our science and engine teams use to model cost-savings recommendations. Every day we ingest and process enormous volumes of metrics and billing data across EC2, Auto Scaling groups, EBS, Lambda, ECS, EKS, RDS/Aurora, DynamoDB, and networking resources — sourcing data from internal systems like CloudWatch, EBS Stats, Lambda Stats, and the Fargate control plane, as well as third-party products such as Datadog. If you enjoy working at the intersection of big data, distributed systems, and real customer impact, this is the place for you.

As a Software Development Engineer on our team, you will:

- Deeply understand the AWS services we optimize — how compute, storage, database, and networking services emit utilization and configuration data — and use that domain knowledge to design a high-throughput, highly available ingestion layer that reliably captures metrics for millions of resources with tight freshness SLAs
- Design, build, and scale data pipelines and services that collect, clean, aggregate, and label huge volumes of metrics with high reliability and low latency
- Own systems end to end — from architecture and implementation to deployment, monitoring, and operations across many regions, including GovCloud and isolated partitions
- Partner with data scientists and engineering teams to define the data they need and deliver it in clean, well-structured, intelligently partitioned data lakes that fuel modeling and recommendations
- Solve hard problems around data security, scalability, and cost efficiency, favoring serverless and decoupled distributed architectures so components scale independently and operational burden stays low
- Establish and meet ingestion and publishing SLAs, build in backfill and data-correction paths, and continuously raise the bar on data quality, operational excellence, and the customer experience

You'll join a collaborative group of engineers who care deeply about doing things the right way — secure by default, reliable at scale, and always focused on the value we deliver to customers. We invest in your growth, give you real ownership from day one, and celebrate the impact you make.

Basic qualifications

- 3+ years of non-internship professional software development experience
- 2+ years of non-internship design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience
- 2+ years of software development engineer or related occupational experience
- 1+ years of designing and developing large-scale, multi-tiered, multi-threaded, embedded or distributed software applications, tools, systems, and services using: C#, C++, Java, or Perl experience
- 1+ years of Object Oriented Design experience
- Bachelor's degree or foreign equivalent in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, or a related field
- Experience programming with at least one software programming language

Preferred qualifications

- 3+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience
- Bachelor's degree in computer science or equivalent

title: Senior Technical Program Manager, Platform Engineering & Emerging Technologies
descriptionHtml:
Drive the programs that bring AWS Secret Cloud for Industry (ASCI) to customers, the managed service that enables cleared U.S. defense contractors and other National Industrial Security Program organizations to run contractor-owned, contractor-operated classified workloads directly on AWS.

As Senior TPM you own the cross-team execution that turns ASCI's roadmap into delivered, adopted capabilities and successful customer onboardings. You run the programs end to end, drive the technical and compliance milestones each launch and onboarding depends on, and keep many teams across AWS, customers, and government stakeholders aligned to the plan. This is a highly technical role that rewards strong program ownership, fluency in technical and compliance detail, and the ability to drive results across organizations without direct authority.

- Own program execution for ASCI launches and customer onboardings, end to end.

- Drive the technical readiness, compliance, and connectivity milestones each delivery depends on.

- Coordinate across AWS service, engineering, security, and field teams, and with customers and government stakeholders.

- Build and run the mechanisms, trackers, and status reporting that keep programs on plan.

- Surface risks and dependencies early, and drive them to resolution.

This position requires that the candidate selected must currently possess and maintain an active TS/SCI security clearance. The position further requires that, after start, the selected candidate obtain and maintain an active TS/SCI security clearance with polygraph or commensurate clearance for each government agency for which they perform AWS work.

Key job responsibilities
- Own programs end to end. Run ASCI's launch and onboarding programs from planning through delivery, holding the schedule, scope, and cross-team commitments.

- Drive technical and compliance milestones. Shepherd each launch and customer onboarding through the readiness, accreditation, and connectivity steps it depends on, keeping them sequenced and unblocked.

- Coordinate across many teams. Align AWS service, engineering, security, and field teams, and work directly with customers and government stakeholders to keep delivery moving.

- Manage risks and dependencies. Identify risks, dependencies, and critical-path blockers early, and drive them to resolution before they slip the plan.

- Build the mechanisms. Create and maintain the trackers, milestone plans, and operating cadence that give the program and its stakeholders a clear, current view of status.

- Report status and drive decisions. Produce concise status, escalations, and program narratives for senior leadership, and run the reviews that keep stakeholders aligned.

Basic qualifications

- 5+ years of technical product or program management experience
- 7+ years of working directly with engineering teams experience
- 3+ years of software development experience
- 5+ years of technical program management working directly with software engineering teams experience
- Experience managing programs across cross functional teams, building processes and coordinating release schedules
- Current, active US Government Security Clearance of Top Secret with SCI eligibility or above

Preferred qualifications

- 5+ years of project management disciplines including scope, schedule, budget, quality, along with risk and critical path management experience
- Experience managing projects across cross functional teams, building sustainable processes and coordinating release schedules
- Experience defining KPI's/SLA's used to drive multi-million dollar businesses and reporting to senior leadership

title: Hardware Development Engineer II, Development Integration and Test
descriptionHtml:
Amazon Leo is Amazon's low Earth orbit satellite network. Our mission is to deliver fast, reliable internet connectivity to customers beyond the reach of existing networks. From individual households to schools, hospitals, businesses, and government agencies, Amazon Leo will serve people and organizations operating in locations without reliable connectivity.

Amazon is building a satellite constellation to deliver broadband connectivity around the world, and our test engineering team is the gate to flight readiness. We are looking for a Hardware Development Engineer II to design and implement test infrastructure for satellite flight hardware, ensuring every component that reaches orbit is proven, reliable, and ready to perform.

In this role, you will develop test systems for mechanical satellite assemblies, working across multiple technology areas to validate designs from early prototypes through production. You will apply your expertise in materials, manufacturing methods, and system integration to build test solutions that catch problems early and confirm hardware meets demanding performance and safety requirements. As we grow to support future generations of satellites, this is a compelling time to join a team where your work directly determines whether hardware is ready to fly.

Export Control Requirement: Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

Key job responsibilities
- Design and develop test infrastructure for satellite flight hardware, producing clear design schematics, specifications, trade studies, and test plans that validate mechanical systems against functional, reliability, and cost targets.
- Build and validate prototypes of test fixtures and equipment, selecting appropriate manufacturing processes and making informed make-versus-buy decisions to meet program schedules.
- Perform system-level analysis including thermal, dynamic, and electrical evaluations to confirm test setups accurately represent flight conditions and meet regulatory and safety requirements.
- Collaborate with cross-functional engineering teams during design reviews, planning discussions, and retrospectives to resolve integration challenges, improve test coverage, and share technical knowledge.
- Develop scripts, firmware, or software tools that automate test workflows, and help train teammates on test system implementation and operation.

A day in the life
You will start your morning reviewing test data from a recent satellite hardware validation run, then join a design review where you present trade-off analyses on a new test fixture to your teammates. After lunch, you might work with a supplier to refine tooling for an upcoming build, or head to the lab to troubleshoot a sensor configuration on a vibration test stand. You will document your findings, propose improvements, and mentor newer engineers along the way.

About the team
Our team designs and operates the test infrastructure that determines whether satellite hardware is ready for flight. We are growing to support future generations of satellites, which means new test challenges and new technology areas to explore. Engineers across mechanical, electrical, and software disciplines work side by side here, and we value clear communication, technical rigor, and a willingness to learn from every test campaign. If you want your work to directly shape what makes it to orbit, this is the team to join.

Basic qualifications

- 4+ years of working in mechanical engineering or equivalent experience
- Experience with prototyping and implementation
- Bachelor's degree in mechanical engineering or equivalent

Preferred qualifications

- Knowledge of SolidWorks simulation or Ansys Finite Element analysis tools
- Experience in the design of complex mechanical products and equipment at volume
- Experience in test setup automation using MATLAB, Python, or Pearl
- Knowledge of industry standard CAD & FEA design tools, industry trends, and design for manufacturability

title: Data Center Technician - 2027 Internship
descriptionHtml:
At Amazon Web Services (AWS), we are working to be the most customer-centric company on earth. To get there, we need exceptionally talented, bright, and driven people. Are you ready to embrace the challenge? Come build the future with us.

This is a unique opportunity to work in some of the most cutting-edge data centers in the world. Amazon data centers are large-scale, high-density facilities where you will help change the face of cloud technology in the region — and your work will directly impact millions of customers.

This internship is designed as a potential pathway to full-time employment. Interns who demonstrate strong performance throughout their internship may be considered for a full-time Data Center Technician position, subject to available roles and business needs.

Who Should Apply

We welcome applications from:

- Students in the last year of their Bachelor's degree in a relevant technical field such as Information Technology, Computer Hardware Repair, or similar. It is a requirement to be graduated by the end of the internship.

Important — Site Location & Commuting: This role is based at a data center facility in a remote location with no public transportation access. A valid driving license and access to personal transportation are required to commute to the site daily. Please consider this before applying.


As a Data Center Technician Intern, you will work as part of the Operations team, whose primary responsibility is the maintenance and upkeep of the data center infrastructure. This position involves hardware and network diagnostics followed by physical repair.

You will be exposed to both independent work and team-based collaboration. Prioritization, organizational skills, effective communication, and the ability to react quickly are critical to being successful.

What You Will Do

You will provide our internal teams with infrastructure-related support, resolving tickets related to hardware (motherboards, Random Access Memory, Central Processing Units, Graphics Processing Units, and more) and networking (link-down events, optics replacements, switch replacements, and more).

In addition to hardware and network repair, you will learn how to install equipment, create documentation, innovate solutions, and fix complex problems within the data center environment.

Your day-to-day duties include:

- Troubleshooting server hardware alongside experienced AWS technicians

- Meeting Service Level Agreements (SLAs) against assigned trouble tickets

- Shadowing AWS technicians during network troubleshooting to build your diagnostic skills

- Replacing media (Solid State Drives and Hard Disk Drives) in accordance with AWS Data Tech guidance

- Performing regular server hardware repairs (drives, motherboards, and other components) under the guidance of experienced technicians

- Interacting with third-party vendors and contractors working on site

Internship Structure

Amazon internships are full-time (40 hours per week) for 3 consecutive months, starting in summer 2027. This position requires the intern to report to work on site daily. Intern schedules are typically day schedules, Sunday through Thursday.

Please note that a full-time Data Center Technician position could involve day, evening, or weekend shifts and on-call rotations. Candidates should be willing and able to commit to shift work upon transitioning to a full-time position.

Diverse Experiences

AWS values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed below, we encourage you to apply. If your career is just starting, has not followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, do not let that stop you from applying.

Your Career at Amazon — A Universe of Opportunity

At Amazon, your career is not a straight path. It is a journey you build as you go.

From your first day as an intern, you will own real work that matters. You will diagnose and repair the servers and networks that keep AWS running for millions of customers. Your mentors and teammates will champion your growth, helping you build skills you did not know existed — and you will see your work come to life at massive scale.

Impact. Your work shapes the infrastructure that millions of customers rely on every day. Every server you repair and every network issue you resolve keeps the cloud running.

Action. You will move fast, learn by doing, and solve real problems from day one. Your ideas do not get stuck in approval chains — they get tested, refined, and put into practice.

Curiosity. Every project teaches you something new. You will apply what you learned in the classroom to real challenges and explore different teams, technologies, and career paths within Amazon.

Mentorship and career growth. You will start with structured onboarding and get paired with experienced mentors. Our team is dedicated to supporting new members in an environment that celebrates knowledge sharing. Projects and tasks are assigned in a way that leverages your strengths and helps you further develop your skill set. Your journey here is yours to shape.

About the team
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. We are the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on.

You will join a diverse team of engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You will collaborate with people across AWS to deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers.

Basic qualifications

- In pursuit of a Bachelor's degree in a relevant technical field such as Information Technology, Computer Hardware Repair, or similar, graduating in 2027 – before the internship´s end date.
- Professional English proficiency, both written and verbal
- Ability to work well with others in a team environment, with strong time management skills

Preferred qualifications

- Basic knowledge of Linux and networking

descriptionHtml:
Summary

The Reliability Maintenance Engineering (RME) team at Amazon is fundamental to our operations – they're the ones keeping vital machinery running at all times. As an RME Technician, you'll maintain a wide range of equipment and workspaces while upholding Health and Safety best practices. You'll help to keep your colleagues safe and prevent machine downtime. Our RME Technicians boost the availability and quality of our equipment and work to enhance the operational environment too.

Shift Pattern: This role includes working in non-traditional shift pattern, which may include nights and weekends






Key job responsibilities
- Proactive and preventative maintenance tasks on a wide range of site equipment
- Carry out reactive repairs and fault diagnosis in a live distribution warehouse
- Use the latest tools to maximise equipment effectiveness
- Uphold all health and safety policies and practices
- Support the development and progression of on-site apprentices
- Work on continuous improvement projects and roll out best practices across a range of EU sites


A day in the life
Our RME Technicians are based on-site, so they can respond quickly to any machinery issues. You'll carry out a range of planned preventative maintenance to our sites' equipment to make sure it's working safely. As an RME Technician, you'll also respond promptly to breakdowns, investigating, finding, and implementing solutions as quickly as possible. You'll also make suggestions for long-term improvements.

Working alongside senior colleagues, you'll undertake day-to-day maintenance tasks and will liaise with contractors if you need external expertise. You'll work on a range of shifts to make sure our sites are supported around the clock – allowing Amazon to deliver at the speed we're known for.

As a Cluster Technician, you'll be assigned a nodal home site that serves as your primary base. However, the role includes an element of travel within your designated cluster of sites. This means you'll move between locations as needed to provide maintenance support, respond to breakdowns, and carry out planned preventative work across multiple facilities. This travel element ensures our sites receive consistent, high-quality technical coverage and gives you the opportunity to broaden your experience across a variety of operational environments.

About the team
Amazon Logistics, or AMZL, handles ‘last mile’ delivery duties in partnership with third-party distribution businesses. We utilise creative thinking and continuous improvement initiatives to get millions of physical products into the hands of our customers. Our goal is to make our customers’ delivery experience as smooth as possible and roll out global delivery solutions for our newest concepts, like Amazon Fresh, Prime Now and Amazon Restaurants.

There are two sides to what we do. Our ‘under the roof’ associates process millions of products for dispatch to our delivery teams. Our team is people-focused and supportive, particularly as lots of our people work through the night. We focus mostly on operations, with 24/7 shifts in most of our locations.

Meanwhile, our ‘on the road’ people work with Amazon Flex - a network of delivery contractors. Every year, we continually raise the bar for customer experience with new, innovative delivery services. We look for new ways to overcome industry wide logistics challenges and new ideas to reduce our carbon footprint, supported by a portfolio of vehicles (including Electric Vehicles) and technology to help us do just that.

- NVQ Level 3/ SVQ Level 3/ IVQ Level 3/ City & Guilds Level 3/EAL Level 3 all specialized in Mechanical, Electrical or Mechatronics

- SVQ Level 3 (or equivalent) in Mechanical, Electrical or Mechatronics, or completed a 4-year UK certified apprenticeship
- Valid Full UK Driving License is Essential

Preferred qualifications

- Associate's degree in Mechnical or Electrical
- Experience with material handling equipment (MHE) safety standards accordance with original equipment manufacturer (OEM) and safety standards
- Experience with robotic operation and maintenance

title: Systems Development Engineer, EC2 Core Platforms Engineering
descriptionHtml:
Build the systems that bring Amazon's newest servers to life. As a Systems Development Engineer on EC2 Core Platforms Engineering, you'll work at the seam between hardware and software to launch new compute platforms, keep the core fleet healthy at massive scale, and automate the way we build.

We own the quality, performance, and reliability of the platforms that host EC2 instances, from lab bring-up through general availability. You'll bring up and validate new EC2 server platforms, working hands-on with Nitro firmware, operating systems, and provisioning, then diagnose and reduce failures across the core fleet to drive reliability. - Help bring up and validate new server platforms that host cloud compute instances, from early lab testing through production launch, working across firmware, operating systems, and hardware.

- Diagnose and reduce hardware and software failures across a large-scale server fleet, using a data-driven, methodical approach to find root causes and drive fixes that improve reliability.

- Build software and automation that streamline how new platforms are introduced, reducing manual effort in provisioning, deployment, and validation so platforms reach production faster and with a high quality bar.

- Develop solutions to difficult problems that span firmware, operating systems, networking, and infrastructure.

- Improve the safety, agility, and automation of the build and launch process, and share what you learn with the team.

- 2+ years of non-internship professional software development experience
- 1+ years of designing or architecting (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience

title: Engineering Operation Technician
descriptionHtml:
Join our dynamic team and become a critical guardian of technological infrastructure! As a Data Center Engineering Technician, you'll play a pivotal role in maintaining the heartbeat of mission-critical technology infrastructure, ensuring seamless operations that power global digital experiences. Your expertise will directly contribute to maintaining an extraordinary 99.999% uptime, keeping the digital world running smoothly and efficiently.

Engineering Technicians are Amazon’s front line when it comes to hands-on electrical and mechanical equipment troubleshooting. They will maintain, operate, and troubleshoot, Data Center Operation’s Mission Critical Facilities, which includes stand-by diesel generators and related fuel systems, as well as three phase electrical systems such as: switch gear, UPSs, PDUs, wet cell batteries and associated systems, CRAC, centrifugal chillers, cooling towers/water chemical system, air handlers and associated systems, pumps, & motors.

AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

NOTE: Amazon does not sponsor for immigration, including for H-1B, TN, and other non-immigrant visas, for this role.
NOTE: Lump sum stipend will be provided to eligible candidates who relocate for this position.



Key job responsibilities
- Daily building rounds to monitor and record information from electrical, mechanical, and fire/life safety equipment to ensure 24/7 reliability and availability
- Monitor Building Management Systems (BMS) and Electrical Power Management System (EPMS)
- Assist in troubleshooting of facility and rack-level events within internal Service Level Agreements (SLA)
- Perform rack installs and rack decommissioning within internal SLA
- Perform PM, troubleshooting, root cause analysis, and repair of electrical and mechanical equipment
- Technical writing to support change management program
- Monitor daily work requests and manage to resolution, and execute projects from conception to completion
- On-site support of contractors, sub-contractors and vendors, ensuring that all work performed is in accordance with established practices, procedures & local legislation
- Work schedule changes depending on specific site needs. Shifts can be up to 12-hours and may rotate on a predefined schedule. Some locations have on-call rotations.
- Role may support more than one location/site.

Physical Requirements:
- Willingness and demonstrated ability to work in the following physical conditions with reasonable accommodations:
- Regularly lift and/or move up to 39 pounds independently
- Participate in group lifts for 40+ pounds
- Maintain balance and perform construction tasks while on a ladder
- Regularly walk, use hands and fingers, handle or feel, reach with hands and arms, stoop, kneel, crouch or crawl, climb stairs, twist, bend, work above shoulders, grasp, carry, push and pull objects into position
- Work in an environment requiring provided ear protection

This role supports data centers in various operational stages. The position may be assigned to a facility still under development, which could require travel to established locations for training until your designated site becomes fully operational.

Essential Requirements:
- Ability to travel to or commute between data center locations as needed
- Willingness to temporarily work at alternative sites during training periods or until assigned facility is operational
- Travel frequency will vary based on business needs and operational status of assigned facility

Candidates must be able to travel (over 50 miles) or commute (less than 50 miles) to active data center sites as required by business needs.



A day in the life
This role acts as Amazon’s front line when it comes to hands-on electrical and mechanical equipment preventative maintenance (PM) and troubleshooting, reporting to a site’s Data Center Facility Manager (FM). They will maintain, operate, and troubleshoot mission-critical data center facility equipment including stand-by diesel generators and related fuel systems, 3 phase electrical systems such as switchgear, UPS units, PDUs, and wet cell batteries and associated systems. Mechanical equipment includes CRAHU units, centrifugal chillers, cooling towers, water systems, air handlers and associated systems, pumps, and motors. Additional support equipment is included in the scope of the role which includes fire/life safety equipment, building automation systems, and general facilities equipment.

- 2+ years of electrical and mechanical facilities maintenance, or 2+ years of electrical facilities maintenance and 1+ years of mechanical facilities maintenance experience
- 2+ years of Microsoft Office products and applications experience
- Work flexible schedule including weekends, nights, and holidays

Preferred qualifications

- 2+ years of data center engineering experience
- Experience reading and writing procedures, technical documents, and engineering drawings

title: Environmental Test Engineer, Amazon Leo
descriptionHtml:
Amazon Leo is building a low Earth orbit satellite constellation to deliver fast, reliable broadband to customers and communities everywhere — including the places the internet has never reliably reached. Every satellite we launch is qualified in our Space Simulation Lab at SEA133. If flight hardware is going to survive launch, vacuum, thermal cycling, and years on orbit, it has to prove it to us first.

Export Control Requirement: Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

As an Environmental Test Engineer on the SSL team, you won't be one of many engineers maintaining a shared pool of equipment. You'll be the primary owner of an entire class of test equipment — Thermal, TVAC, Vibe, Shock, or HASS — accountable for keeping it running, driving its reliability upward, and building the processes that let the lab test at launch cadence. When something goes wrong at 2 AM, your name is on the escalation. When something needs to change, you own the engineering decision and the vendor conversation. When a technician learns the equipment, they learn it from you.

This is a build job, not a maintain job. We're scaling SSL fast and we need an engineer who looks at tribal knowledge and turns it into standard work; who looks at a vendor's response time and decides it's not good enough; who can read a thermal ramp trace or a shaker response curve and tell you whether it's a tuning problem, a hardware problem, or a software problem. You will have autonomy, a direct line to leadership, and a tangible connection between the work you do this week and the hardware that leaves Earth next quarter.

If you want your engineering decisions to show up in orbit — not just in a dashboard — come build this with us.

Key job responsibilities
Equipment Ownership
• Serve as primary owner for an assigned class of environmental test equipment (Thermal, TVAC, Vibe, Shock, or HASS), managing configurations, maintenance, calibration, and improvement projects.
• Provide technical leadership during troubleshooting events, driving issues from first response through root cause and corrective action.
• Manage relationships with 3rd-party equipment vendors (service, spares, upgrades, escalations).
Process Development
• Establish standardized test processes and work instructions that enable technicians to operate with minimal engineer supervision.
• Train and mentor technicians on equipment operation and troubleshooting; keep documentation accurate and current.
Rate Improvement
• Analyze test data to validate ability of test procedures to meet requirements.
• Identify and lead projects that increase throughput, reduce cycle time, and improve first-pass yield.
Automation Troubleshooting
• Read and triage simple errors in LabVIEW and Python code execution; clearly articulate failures to support teams for more complex issues.
• Apply understanding of control loops used in environmental test (thermal ramp control, vacuum/pressure control, shaker control) to diagnose equipment behavior.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, or an equivalent field
- Experience in complex work environments, including (but not limited to robotics, automation, diagnostic and test equipment)
- Experience troubleshooting and debugging technical systems, or experience that includes strong analytical skills, attention to detail, and effective communication abilities and experience with automation and any version control tools
- Knowledge of industry standard test automation tools and experience developing product test frameworks
- Experience in reliability/maintenance environments, or experience communicating technical concepts to non-technical audiences

Preferred qualifications

- Master's degree or above in engineering or equivalent
- 3+ years of hardware development, test lab, space/aerospace maintenance or hands-on engineering environment experience
- Experience reading and interpreting construction drawings and specifications, or experience leading technical teams through daily operations and maintenance evolutions
- Experience working with and managing third party vendors, or experience in planning, scheduling and auditing maintenance activities
- Experience leading cross-functional projects and implementing strategic initiatives
- Experience with Industrial control systems, both hardware and software
- 2+ years of supporting procedures for production or mission critical environments to include ticketing, monitoring/metrics, and troubleshooting technical issues experience

descriptionHtml:
Leo is Amazon’s low Earth orbit satellite broadband network. Its mission is to deliver fast, reliable internet to customers and communities around the world, and we’ve designed the system with the capacity, flexibility, and performance to serve a wide range of customers, from individual households to schools, hospitals, businesses, government agencies, and other organizations operating in locations without reliable connectivity.

Export Control: This position requires that the candidate selected be a U.S. Citizen in order to comply with U.S. government-imposed requirements related to the nature of the work and/or where it will be performed.

Key job responsibilities
- Program Leadership: Lead large-scale, complex technical programs across multiple teams and disciplines, from inception to delivery
- Strategic Planning: Develop and execute comprehensive program plans aligned with Leo's mission and business objectives
- Cross-functional Coordination: Orchestrate efforts across engineering, operations, product, and business teams to ensure seamless program execution
- Risk Management: Identify, assess, and mitigate risks that could impact program success, developing contingency plans as needed
- Stakeholder Management: Build and maintain relationships with senior leadership, external partners, and regulatory bodies, ensuring clear communication and alignment
- Technical Expertise: Leverage technical understanding to facilitate decision-making and problem-solving across teams
- Process Improvement: Implement and optimize program management methodologies to increase efficiency and scalability
- Metrics and Reporting: Develop and maintain program KPIs, providing regular updates to leadership on progress, risks, and outcomes

A day in the life
As a Technical Program Manager on the Leo Devices & Systems Infrastructure team, you'll drive the development and operations programs for service environments and ServiceNow. Your day involves leading and being a part of cross-functional stand-with stakeholders, shared service owners, security and export compliance while collaborating with engineering leads to address technical challenges. You'll analyze fleet health metrics and compliance data to guide program decisions, present status updates to leadership, and coordinate with external partners like ServiceNow and Taninum. The role requires balancing immediate operational demands with long-term strategic planning, all within a regulated environment.

About the team
You will be part of the Leo Devices & Systems Infrastructure team who is responsible for the lifecycle of service environments for manufacturing and design functions along with ServiceNow at Leo. You will lead implementation programs for which the team has ownership in delivery of the outcome with programs ranging from deploying new software to transformation of existing services. In addition, we own ServiceNow for Leo for which you will lead implementation tracks along that service’s roadmap. You and your team will play a crucial role in Leo's mission to deliver reliable internet globally through innovative device management solutions and automation.

Basic qualifications

- 5+ years of technical product or program management experience
- 7+ years of working directly with engineering teams experience
- 5+ years of analytical, quantitative, communication, and presentations experience
- Experience leading highly technical programs involving infrastructure, complex systems, systems engineering
- Experience managing technical programs across cross-functional teams, building processes and coordinating release schedules

Preferred qualifications

- 5+ years of project management disciplines including scope, schedule, budget, quality, along with risk and critical path management experience
- Experience defining KPI's/SLA's used to drive multi-million dollar businesses and reporting to senior leadership
- Experience in technical program management working directly with software engineering teams

descriptionHtml:
There’s a universe of opportunity at Amazon.

At Amazon, your career doesn’t follow a straight line. It accelerates, twists, and challenges you in ways you never expected. From the moment you join, you’re part of something big: building products or services that reach millions and shaping how people live, work, and connect every day. This is where your ideas turn into real impact. You’ll work with world class tools, global platforms, and systems built to operate at an extraordinary scale. You’ll move fast, experiment and launch solutions that matter. With endless pportunities to explore across teams and roles, you’ll learn quickly, apply what you know and discover skills you didn’t know existed. This is an environment designed for builders who want to see the impact of their work in the world. Ready to start your adventure?


What’s in it for you?

An internship at Amazon means real responsibility from day one. You’ll build, test, and learn alongside people who want to see you succeed, while making an impact that reaches far beyond campus.

Key job responsibilities
Amazon is looking for ambitious, curious and versatile individuals to join our unique world as interns. Our Amazon internship will provide you with an exceptional opportunity to experience a fast-paced, dynamic and internationally diverse environment; it will boost your resume, and provide a superb introduction to our daily responsibilities. We are looking for a highly driven, entrepreneurial, analytical and customer-obsessed Business Developer Intern. You will join the team before the launch of a new service offering and will contribute to the development of a strong pipeline, and to collecting market segment and customer insights to improve the product and delight the Amazon customers. You are the ideal candidate if:

- You are excited by contributing to launching and help developing a new business

- You love to identify and interact with current and potential future customers, listen to their needs, and work to find the best solutions for them

- You are a self-starter, and can juggle multiple priorities to make things happen in a fast-paced, dynamic, and often highly ambiguous environment

- You are able to help manage the relationship with partners and prospects, and meet and exceed program goals.

- You are able to translate customer needs into product requirements

- You can easily shift from strategic thinking to rolling up your sleeves and executing, in order to deliver results

Key job responsibilities:

- Deliver Results: Identify market segment opportunities for our new service offering.

- Customer relationship management: Building and maintaining strong, trustful relationship with our potential future customers

- Cross-functional collaboration: Relay market segment needs and requirements back to internal Amazon teams including Product Management and Tech teams

- Dive deep: Measure performance, articulate root-cause analysis, and link to specific improvement areas

- Invent and Simplify: Analyze current purchasing processes and evaluate opportunities for solutions to improve end user experiences, reduce costs, and accelerate organization performance

A day in the life
As an intern, you will be matched to a mentor.

In addition to learning about an impactful project, you will have the opportunity to engage with Amazonians for both personal and professional
development, expand your network, and participate in activities with other interns throughout your internship.

No matter the location of your internship,
we give you the tools to own your project and learn in a real-world setting.
About the team
If you’re insatiably curious and always want to learn more, then you’ve come to the right place. Depending on your location, country, job status and other requirements, some or all of the following benefits may be available to you as an intern.

- Competitive pay
- Impactful project and internship/role deliverables
- Networking opportunities with fellow interns

- Mentorship and career development

Internship length is 12 months, full-time.

Intern Community:

You'll collaborate with interns from around the world, networking and participating in social events to broaden your perspectives. You can also join specialized groups focused on areas like sustainability to explore your diverse interests.

- The internship program provides a robust support system, including weekly intern office hours, dedicated IT and HR support, and a program team committed to your success. This ensures you have the guidance and assistance needed to thrive.

Learning Sessions:

- Exclusive learning sessions will further enhance your skills, granting you access to Amazon's learning platforms and the expertise of industry leaders. These structured development opportunities will prepare you for the next step in your career.

Opportunities:

- Upon successful completion of the internship, you may be considered for a graduate role or a second internship, allowing you to continue your journey with Amazon. Additionally, you'll enjoy a competitive monthly salary, relocation support, and access to a range of employee benefits.



Available to commence an internship in Q1 2027.

You should be available for 12 months, full time (40h/week) in Cape Town.

title: Software Development Engineer II, Silicon Scan & Fleet Diagnostics, Machine Learning Accelerator Technology Team
descriptionHtml:
Annapurna Labs designs silicon and software that accelerates innovation. Customers choose us to create cloud solutions that solve challenges that were unimaginable a short time ago—even yesterday. Our custom chips, accelerators, and software stacks enable us to take on technical challenges that have never been seen before, and deliver results that help our customers change the world.

In Annapurna Labs we are at the forefront of hardware/software co-design not just in Amazon Web Services (AWS) but across the industry. The MLA Technology team is looking for candidates who are excited to write software that tests silicon itself—running structural scan (DFT) tests across a huge fleet of machine learning accelerator servers, and turning the results into insights about some of the largest chips ever built.

Do you like the idea of testing billions of transistors and finding the one that’s misbehaving? Great! Ever talked to a chip over JTAG just to see what it would say? Great! Do you read data sheets like others read the news? Great! Written a script to automate something tedious, then kept improving it just because you could? Great! Enjoy turning a mountain of raw data into a dashboard that tells a story? Great! Did this make you smile? Awesome.

Our team writes software that tests the most advanced machine learning chips in the world, at a scale and speed few systems anywhere can match. If that interests you, come join our team!

Key job responsibilities
- Own and evolve the software that speeds up structural scan (DFT) test execution across a large fleet of ML accelerator servers
- Design and deliver improvements to the tools and workflows used to bring new scan test patterns to production, from architecture through deployment
- Build data analytics and dashboards that track test pattern execution across the fleet
- Automate silicon debug and large-scale investigation workflows
- Partner with the teams that run and validate scan testing at scale, turning their needs into maintainable, tested, reusable software
- Mentor early-career engineers and raise the bar through design discussions and thorough, but kind, code reviews

A day in the life
As an SDE II on the team, you’ll own problems end to end—designing the solution, writing the code, testing it against real hardware, and shipping it to a fleet. One day you might be profiling scan execution to shave seconds off a test that runs across thousands of machines; another day you might be building a dashboard that shows how a new test pattern is behaving across the fleet, or automating complex silicon investigations. No software is too low level for us. No software is too high level for us. You’ll work alongside senior engineers deep in silicon test, and help early-career engineers on the team grow through your designs and code reviews.

About the team
We are not a team of machine learning practitioners—we are a software team focused on testing and understanding the silicon that enables accelerated machine learning workloads at scale, including the chips behind AWS Trainium and AWS Inferentia.

Our team is dedicated to supporting new members. We have a broad mix of experience levels and tenures, and we’re building an environment that celebrates knowledge-sharing and mentorship. Our senior members enjoy one-on-one mentoring and thorough, but kind, code reviews. We care about your career growth and strive to assign projects that help you develop your engineering expertise so you feel empowered to take on more complex tasks in the future.

Basic qualifications

- 3+ years of non-internship professional software development experience
- 2+ years of non-internship design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience
- Experience programming with at least one software programming language

Preferred qualifications

- 3+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience
- Bachelor's degree in computer science or equivalent
- Experience in embedded development in C/C++
- Knowledge of computer architecture, operating systems, and parallel computing
- Experience writing low level drivers
- Experience in debugging, profiling, and implementing software engineering best practices in large-scale systems

title: Systems Development Engineer, Lab Operations Platform, Amazon Leo DevOps
descriptionHtml:
Amazon Leo is Amazon’s low Earth orbit satellite broadband network. Its mission is to deliver fast, reliable internet to customers and communities around the world, and we’ve designed the system with the capacity, flexibility, and performance to serve a wide range of customers, from individual households to schools, hospitals, businesses, government agencies, and other organizations operating in locations without reliable connectivity.

Satellite development moves fast, and the labs that support it never have enough hands for every request. The Amazon Leo Development Operations (DevOps) team runs the labs where spacecraft hardware is built, tested, and qualified, and the right call on any given day depends on knowing exactly what work is waiting, who can do it, and which equipment is ready. Today that picture is assembled by hand. We are looking for a Systems Development Engineer to build the systems that replace it.

You will own the software that connects our lab personnel, lab spaces, and lab equipment, and you will turn scattered scheduling, ticketing, and equipment data into clear, trusted views of capacity and demand. Our lab engineers and technicians are not software developers, so what you build has to be intuitive enough that they want to use it. Over time, the same tools will show which equipment is available and ready, so planning covers people, spaces, and equipment together. Your work will help lab leadership make faster priority calls and keep our design-team customers supported on the most urgent, actionable work.

Export Control Requirement: Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

Key job responsibilities
• Own the software systems that interface with lab personnel, lab spaces, and lab equipment, from design through operation
• Design and build tools and dashboards that visualize lab personnel and equipment capacity against design-team demand
• Integrate data from headcount and scheduling, customer priority input, Jira work ticketing, engineer work estimates, equipment maintenance, and equipment data logging into a consistent backend data model
• Build and maintain APIs that connect Jira, our in-house tools, and systems owned by other teams
• Design interfaces that non-software users can pick up without training, and work directly with lab engineers and lab management to iterate on them
• Bring lab equipment into the same tools, surfacing equipment status and availability so that people can visualize it and plan their work around it
• Ensure test and equipment data is stored securely, kept clean, and remains traceable and usable
• Navigate Amazon security reviews, data classification, and compliance requirements for all systems you build and operate
• Start with clear, reliable visualizations of current capacity and demand, and evolve them into forecasting and planning tools
• Partner with equipment-focused engineers and teams across the organization to converge lab personnel and lab equipment tooling into a single system over time
• Operate what you build: write documentation and runbooks, monitor system health, and drive permanent fixes when things break


A day in the life
You will spend your time between the lab floor and the codebase. One day you might sit with a lab engineer to watch how they report work estimates, then turn that into a simpler input form. Another day you might design the data model that joins ticket status changes with technician schedules, or connect equipment status and availability into the same tools so engineers can see what is ready and plan their work around it. You might also work through a security review for a new integration. You will work closely with lab management, who rely on your tools to decide where to point limited people, and with the engineers who maintain our equipment systems.

About the team
The Amazon Leo Development Operations (DevOps) team supports the full arc of satellite development, from prototyping through development builds, testing, and qualification. We keep the labs, equipment, and technical infrastructure that Amazon Leo’s hardware engineers depend on running. Our labs are in our Redmond facilities. We are a small, hands-on team that thrives in a fast-paced, start-up-like environment, and we value people who find a gap, own it, and close it.
We are building our lab software capability from the ground up. You will have real ownership, direct access to the people who use your work, and room to shape how Amazon Leo understands and manages its development labs.

Basic qualifications

- Experience programming with at least one modern language such as Python, Ruby, Golang, Java, C++, C#, Rust
- Experience with Linux/Unix
- Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, a related field, or equivalent experience
- 5+ years of professional software and systems development experience
- Experience using analytics and presenting data to make decisions
- Experience designing and delivering internal tools or applications end to end, including both front-end and back-end components
- Experience designing data models and building APIs or data pipelines that integrate multiple source systems
- Experience with SQL and relational or non-relational data stores
- Experience building software that models or manages physical operations, such as scheduling, resource allocation, inventory, equipment, or facilities workflows
- Experience gathering requirements from non-technical users and delivering usable, intuitive interfaces
- Experience operating production systems, including documentation, monitoring, and troubleshooting
