title: DCO Tech Intern
descriptionHtml:
At Amazon Web Services (AWS), we are working to be the most customer-centric company on earth. To get there, we need exceptionally talented, bright, and driven people. Are you ready to embrace the challenge? Come build the future with us.

This is a unique opportunity to work in some of the most cutting-edge data centers in the world. Amazon data centers are large-scale, high-density facilities where you will help change the face of cloud technology in the region — and your work will directly impact millions of customers.

This internship is designed as a potential pathway to full-time employment. Interns who demonstrate strong performance throughout their internship may be considered for a full-time Data Center Technician position, subject to available roles and business needs.

Who Should Apply

We welcome applications from:

- Students who have completed — or due to complete before the internship end date — a higher education qualification (National Qualifications Framework level 4 to 6) or a Bachelor's degree in a relevant technical field such as Information Technology, Computer Hardware Repair, or similar

Important — Site Location & Commuting: This role is based at a data center facility in a remote location with no public transportation access. A valid driving license and access to personal transportation are required to commute to the site daily. Please consider this before applying.

About the Role

As a Data Center Technician Intern, you will work as part of the Operations team, whose primary responsibility is the maintenance and upkeep of the data center's computer and network infrastructure. This position involves hardware and network diagnostics followed by physical repair.

You will be exposed to both independent work and team-based collaboration. Prioritization, organizational skills, effective communication, and the ability to react quickly are critical to being successful.

What You Will Do

You will provide our internal teams with infrastructure-related support, resolving tickets related to hardware (motherboards, Random Access Memory, Central Processing Units, Graphics Processing Units, and more) and networking (link-down events, optics replacements, switch replacements, and more).

In addition to hardware and network repair, you will learn how to install equipment, create documentation, innovate solutions, and fix complex problems within the data center environment.

Your day-to-day duties include:

- Troubleshooting server hardware alongside experienced AWS technicians
- Meeting Service Level Agreements (SLAs) against assigned trouble tickets
- Shadowing AWS technicians during network troubleshooting to build your diagnostic skills
- Replacing media (Solid State Drives and Hard Disk Drives) in accordance with AWS Data Tech guidance
- Performing regular server hardware repairs (drives, motherboards, and other components) under the guidance of experienced technicians
Interacting with third-party vendors and contractors working on site

A day in the life: Watch a day in the life of a Data Center Technician

Internship Structure

Amazon internships are full-time (40 hours per week) for six consecutive months, starting in March/April 2027. This position requires the intern to report to work on site daily. Intern schedules are typically day schedules, Monday through Friday.

Please note that a full-time Data Center Technician position could involve day, evening, or weekend shifts and on-call rotations. Candidates should be willing and able to commit to shift work upon transitioning to a full-time position.

Amazon does not sponsor immigration for this role.

South Africa Employment Equity Requirements

In line with applicable legislation, preference will be given to eligible applicants from designated groups (that is, Black people (used as a collective term for Africans, Colored, Indians and Chinese) women, and persons with disabilities who are citizens of South Africa). Appointments will be made on merit and in accordance with organizational requirements).
- Be a South African citizen with a valid Identity Document
- Unemployed before joining the internship program.
- Age requirement: below 35 years
- Must have completed a higher education qualification in a related field (Minimum NQF level 4-6 qualification)
- Qualification must be from an accredited institution of higher education

Diverse Experiences

AWS values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed below, we encourage you to apply. If your career is just starting, has not followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, do not let that stop you from applying.

Your Career at Amazon — A Universe of Opportunity

At Amazon, your career is not a straight path. It is a journey you build as you go.

From your first day as an intern, you will own real work that matters. You will diagnose and repair the servers and networks that keep AWS running for millions of customers. Your mentors and teammates will champion your growth, helping you build skills you did not know existed — and you will see your work come to life at a massive scale.

Impact. Your work shapes the infrastructure that millions of customers rely on every day. Every server you repair and every network issue you resolve keeps the cloud running.

Action. You will move fast, learn by doing, and solve real problems from day one. Your ideas do not get stuck in approval chains — they get tested, refined, and put into practice.

Curiosity. Every project teaches you something new. You will apply what you learned in the classroom to real challenges and explore different teams, technologies, and career paths within Amazon.

Mentorship and career growth. You will start with structured onboarding and get paired with experienced mentors. Our team is dedicated to supporting new members in an environment that celebrates knowledge sharing. Projects and tasks are assigned in a way that leverages your strengths and helps you further develop your skill set. Your journey here is yours to shape.


About the team
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. We are the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on.

You will join a diverse team of engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You will collaborate with people across AWS to deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers.

title: Investigation Specialist, Trust & Safety
descriptionHtml:
In this role, you’ll be the person who keeps our delivery ecosystem honest, safe, and running smoothly. You’ll investigate issues that could impact drivers or customers, spot patterns before they turn into real problems, and bring clarity to situations that often feel messy or ambiguous. What sets this position apart is the blend of analytical thinking and people-centered judgement: you’ll dive into facts, speak with the right stakeholders, and guide decisions that affect the overall health of our delivery partners. If you enjoy solving problems that matter, protecting people, and building mechanisms that make operations better every day, this role puts you right at the heart of it.

Key job responsibilities
• Look into reported incidents and uncover what really happened by gathering facts, interviewing stakeholders, and analyzing available data.
• Drive fair and consistent decision-making when issues arise, ensuring both drivers’ rights and business expectations are respected.
• Identify early warning signs, behavioral trends, recurring violations, or gaps in compliance—and take action before problems escalate.
• Work closely with operational teams and DSP to explain findings, agree on corrective steps, and monitor follow-through.
• Help build simple mechanisms and routines that prevent repeated issues and make the overall ecosystem safer and more reliable.
• Prepare clear summaries and recommendations that help leaders act quickly and confidently.
• Support escalations when needed, especially in situations that could affect safety, customer experience, or business continuity.
• Maintain balanced judgement in sensitive or time-pressured cases, ensuring fairness and consistency at all times.


A day in the life
Your day starts with reviewing any new incidents that came in overnight. You look at the facts, reach out to the right people, and assess whether anything needs urgent attention. You might spend part of the morning speaking Stakeholders to understand what went wrong in a recent situation, or walking them through the actions they need to take next.
Later in the day, you dig into patterns, maybe a location has repeated complaints, or a partner shows early signs of non-compliance. You connect with field teams, ask direct questions, and help them see what needs to change.
Some days are calm; others involve navigating sensitive topics or guiding teams through decisions. Throughout, your goal stays the same: protect people, protect the customer experience, and keep the delivery network healthy, fair, and functioning smoothly.


About the team
The Network Health (NH) and Trust & Safety (T&S) teams work together to protect Amazon’s Last Mile operations by driving compliance, partner accountability, and safety across the AMET region (UAE, Saudi Arabia, Egypt, and Turkey).

Network Health owns the end-to-end compliance and enforcement lifecycle for Delivery Service Partners (DSPs) — from risk identification and MEP (Monitoring & Enforcement Plan) management to exit governance and performance reviews. The team ensures that all DSPs operate safely, ethically, and in alignment with Amazon’s Supply Chain Standards and local labor regulations.

Trust & Safety complements this work by focusing on driver-level safety, identity verification, and incident resolution programs such as Sentinel, DWEL, and DAF, ensuring that both DSPs and drivers uphold Amazon’s zero-tolerance standards on compliance and worker welfare.

Basic qualifications

- 1+ years of customer service experience
- Speak, write, and read fluently in English
- Experience with Microsoft Office products and applications
- Work a flexible schedule/shift/work area, including weekends, nights, and/or holidays
- Experience in payments or e-commerce
- Experience working with Microsoft Office tools (Excel, Word, Outlook, etc.)

Preferred qualifications

- Experience in investigation is a plus

title: Applied Scientist, Amazon Ads
descriptionHtml:
Amazon Ads runs one of the largest real-time decision systems in the world. To meet advertiser goals, we process >4 million ad requests per second, and this team decides which of them are worth the compute. We mine a petabyte-scale stream of traffic to tell in-demand, valuable requests apart from wasteful ones, filtering out the noise and forwarding only what brings value to advertisers, all within milli-seconds. Our solutions save millions in compute costs and drive long-term growth for Amazon's Retail and Marketplace businesses.

Why you'll love this role: The scientific challenge here is scale and signal: large-scale ML on enormous, high-velocity data, optimization and auction dynamics, and causal measurement of what actually moves the business. Generative AI and LLMs are tools you reach for when they help, not the point of the work. The impact also reaches beyond Amazon: we donated the Dynamic Traffic Engine (DTE) to the IAB Tech Lab as an open-source framework that lets demand-side platforms signal which bid requests they value, so supply-side platforms send fewer wasteful ones and QPS waste drops across the whole programmatic supply chain. We are a highly motivated, collaborative team with an entrepreneurial spirit and a broad mandate to experiment and innovate. You will work alongside talented engineers, product managers, and scientists in a culture that rewards bias for action, innovation, and experimentation. What makes this role unique is the combination of scientific rigor with real-world impact at a scale very few systems reach.

Your impact and career growth: Amazon Ads is investing heavily in AI and ML, creating room for scientists to innovate and make their mark. As an Applied Scientist, you will own the science for well-defined supply-optimization problems and take your work end to end, from framing the approach through experimentation and into production with measured business impact. You will partner closely with engineers to productionize your models and with product managers to tie your science to customer and advertiser outcomes. You will share your findings, begin to mentor teammates, and grow your influence on the team's technical direction over time. This is your opportunity to do high-rigor applied science in one of the fastest-growing businesses at Amazon.

Learn more about Amazon Ads: https://advertising.amazon.com/

Key job responsibilities
As an Applied Scientist in Amazon Ads, you will:

- Conduct hands-on data analysis and build large-scale ML models and pipelines for supply optimization.
- Take your models end to end, from proof of concept through experimentation, optimization, and deployment into production, working closely with software engineers to productionize them and with product managers and fellow scientists along the way.
- Design and run A/B experiments and causal analysis to validate hypotheses, draw insights from petabyte-scale data, and measure real business impact.
- Research and apply advanced ML, including generative AI and large language models, to demand prediction and traffic filtering.
- Drive end-to-end optimization projects that tackle ambiguous problems at massive scale, developing scalable, efficient processes for model development, validation, and deployment that optimize traffic monetization while maintaining customer experience.

Basic qualifications

- 3+ years of building models for business application experience
- PhD, or Master's degree and 4+ years of CS, CE, ML or related field experience
- Experience programming in Java, C++, Python or related language
- Experience in any of the following areas: algorithms and data structures, parsing, numerical optimization, data mining, parallel and distributed computing, high-performance computing

Preferred qualifications

- Experience using Unix/Linux
- Experience in professional software development

title: PCIe Validation Engineer, SPIV team
descriptionHtml:
Annapurna Labs designs the custom silicon and systems at the heart of AWS (Amazon Web Services). Here you'll move like a startup, build at the scale of the world's largest cloud, and push the limits of what hardware can do.

Annapurna Labs, as part of Amazon, is looking for a PCIe Validation Engineer.

As a PCIe Validation Engineer, you’ll validate PCIe interfaces of the newest generations on our new products across the full product lifecycle — from early silicon bring-up through manufacturing test integration. You’ll join a validation team responsible for PCIe link quality across all AWS server platforms, ensuring our custom Hosts and smart NICs perform flawlessly before reaching millions of customers.

In this role you will define and execute validation plans for PCIe interfaces across multiple ASIC generations and server platforms. You will verify silicon, firmware, and retimer functionality against design specifications, and drive complex system-level debugs spanning hardware, firmware, and software. You will work with PCIe IP vendors, retimer and switch vendors, and platform integration teams to ensure interoperability and link quality. You will set high standards for yourself and your work, continuously looking for ways to improve the quality and reliability of our products. We are transforming an industry, and we are looking for individuals who are ready for this challenge and want to reach beyond what is possible today.

Key job responsibilities
- Define and execute validation plans for PCIe interfaces on new ASIC generations, covering card-level and server-level link validation across multiple server platforms
- Validate interoperability with third-party PCIe components including, PCIe switches, and PHY IP from silicon vendors,
- Support manufacturing test integration — define and refine PCIe test criteria for contract manufacturers, analyze yield data, and drive feedback loops to improve product quality
- Investigate and root-cause PCIe link failures, error patterns, and performance anomalies at the system level — spanning NIC firmware, host BIOS/BMC, and kernel drivers
- Support RMA analysis — reproduce field failures on returned hardware, classify PCIe-related root causes, and feed findings back to design and firmware teams

About the team
Our SPIV team owns the performance and reliability of PCIe and Ethernet across every AWS server. We work end-to-end across the full product lifecycle, including:
• Pre-silicon IP vendor engagement
• post-silicon bring-up and interface optimization
• SerDes, firmware, and system-level debug
• Interface manufacturing test integration
• Fleet health monitoring and customer performance
• Interoperability with third-party components - retimer, switch, active cable, and optics
In partnership with chip design, Server design and Cloud health teams, you will validate new server platform generations; root-cause failures across hardware, firmware, and software boundaries and drive quality improvements that protect millions of customer workloads.
If you are a systems, hardware, or software engineer who thrives at the intersection of silicon, firmware, and server infrastructure — and wants your work to improve reliability across a global fleet — apply now.

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or equivalent.
- 4+ years of hands-on hardware validation experience at the board or system level.
- 2+ years of experience with high-speed interface validation and debug.
- Working knowledge of Python scripting and Linux environments

Preferred qualifications

- Demonstrated expertise with PCIe protocol, including link training, LTSSM state machine, equalization, lane margining, and error classification (AER/RAS-DES)
- Proficiency with Linux, boot sequences, BIOS/BMC interfaces, and remote system debugging
- Lab experience with racks, cabling, interconnects, and physical server infrastructure
- Experience with manufacturing test environments — defining test criteria, analyzing yield data, and working with contract manufacturers

title: Senior Account SA, AGS Tech
descriptionHtml:
This is the role where architecture meets impact. The Account Solutions Architect (SA) is the trusted technical advisor that customers rely on from first engagement through production and beyond - building sustained technical relationships, understanding customer objectives, and guiding them toward solutions that deliver measurable business outcomes. Through ongoing technical credibility and a commitment to the customer's success, the Account SA drives adoption and deepens engagement in ways that produce lasting business outcomes as the enduring technical voice that earns and maintains customer trust as a member of the account team.

​​The Account SA validates recommendations through hands-on building, turning architectural insight into working solutions that earn customer trust.​

The Account SA provides prescriptive technical guidance - selecting services, designing secure, resilient and scalable architectures, optimizing for cost and performance, and surfacing risks early. Operates as a hands-on builder in the customer's [non-production] environment, validating solutions through working proof points (PoCs, prototypes, reference implementations) because working solutions earn trust that documents cannot. The role scales impact beyond individual engagements by contributing reusable assets other practitioners adopt, orchestrating access to deeper expertise when needed, and transferring capability so customers achieve self-sufficiency rather than dependency.

Key job responsibilities
Technical Solution Design & Customer Advisory
- Designs secure end-to-end solutions for customer workloads, making trade-off decisions across scalability, reliability, performance, cost, and operational efficiency while navigating constraints, operational maturity, and competing business priorities.
- Acts as a trusted technical advisor to the customer's technical and business stakeholders, understanding business objectives, technology landscape, and industry context to recommend fit-for-purpose solutions that connect architectural decisions to long-term business outcomes.
- Advances customer decisions across complex stakeholder groups by making business outcomes (cost reduction, time-to-value, return on investment) tangible and credible through the appropriate combination of architectural reasoning, technical proof, or working demonstrations.
- Evaluates existing customer architectures to identify gaps, risks, modernization and optimization opportunities; delivers actionable remediation guidance and modernization roadmaps.

Building & Demonstrating Solutions
- Operates as a hands-on builder who develops and validates solutions through working proof points in own sandbox and customer non-production environments - leveraging emerging technologies and AI-assisted development to accelerate proof-of-value delivery while maintaining security and operational rigor.
- Applies a production mindset from the outset, integrating governance, security, resiliency, observability, and human validation of critical deliverables into all demonstrable artifacts. Delivers solutions to Amazon Coding Bar (technical standards): tested, secure, and maintainable by others.

Cross-Functional Collaboration
- ​​Partners with sales, business development, professional services, support, product/engineering teams, and external partners teams to move solutions from adoption through launch, orchestrating multi-team delivery against a shared architecture.​
- Provides technical input to product teams by translating customer evidence into clear, actionable requirements that tighten the feedback loop between Account engagements and product direction.

Enablement & Organizational Development
- Improves how the team operates by driving process changes, knowledge transfer, mentoring others, leading design reviews, creating reusable assets (code, tooling, reference implementations) that scale best practices, and recruiting technical talent to sustain a high-performing team.

Thought Leadership & Content Development
- Develops and delivers prescriptive technical content - reference architectures, workshops, white papers, blog posts, and presentations - that shifts how other technical practitioners deliver and educates the broader technical community.
- Represents the organization at industry events, customer forums, and technical conferences as a recognized technical voice.

Recommended Functional Skills

AI-Assisted Development & Tooling, Data Engineering, Emerging Technology Fluency, Hands-on Building & Proof-of-Concept Development, Instructional Design, Sales Presentation / Sales Solution Creation, Software Development & Code Delivery, System Architecture, Technical Communication, Technology & Security Architecture

A day in the life
Your day starts with context - reviewing where your customers are in their technical journey, what's changed in their environment, and what's next. You might open with a design session where you're whiteboarding architecture options with a customer's engineering team, making trade-off decisions together, and committing to a direction. By mid-morning, you're building - writing code, deploying infrastructure, or extending a proof of concept in a sandbox to validate what you recommended yesterday.

After lunch, you're in a customer strategy session with your account team - advising on technical direction, connecting technical progress to business outcomes, navigating competing priorities, and aligning on what proof point will give the customer's decision-makers confidence to move forward. Not everything is clear-cut; you often work with incomplete information, shifting requirements, and stakeholders who don't yet agree on the problem - and you move things forward anyway.

Your week includes time you protect for keeping current - whether that's tracking emerging technologies, following industry shifts, or getting hands-on with a new service before a customer asks about it. You invest in the broader SA community too: mentoring a newer SA through a complex engagement or publishing a reference architecture from a recent win so others don't start from scratch. Travel is part of the rhythm - you're on-site with customers as the role requires, varying by geography and customer portfolio, because trust is built faster in person and the best architectural decisions happen at the whiteboard, not over email.

About the team
Diverse Experiences
AWS values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Our inclusion events foster stronger, more collaborative teams. Our continual innovation is fueled by the bold ideas, fresh perspectives, and passionate voices our teams bring to everything we do.

Mentorship & Career Growth
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve.

- 3+ years of design, implementation, or consulting in applications and infrastructures experience

title: InfraOps Support Engineer, Operations Management Center (OMC)
descriptionHtml:
The InfraOps Support Engineer is a Tier 1 support engineer in Amazon's Operations Management Center (OMC) - a 24/7/365 team that keeps the technology inside Amazon's 400+ corporate office buildings running across Networking, Audio-Visual (AV), and Print services. This engineer is the first line of response for office-infrastructure incidents.

Operating within the Amazon Support Engineer (SupEng) job family, the engineer provides high-quality support across all three service areas while beginning to develop deep subject-matter expertise in one or more focus areas, for which they become the technical point of contact on their team. They respond, triage and resolve incidents within target times using established procedures, detect trends before they become problems, contribute to and refine the team's operating procedures, and mentor more junior engineers. Success requires the ability to work in a fast-paced, collaborative, shift-based environment.

Key job responsibilities
On a typical shift, an InfraOps Support Engineer will:

1. Monitor, Detect & Triage

Be the first line of response and keep ahead of problems.

Triage incoming incidents (tickets) within defined target response times, using judgment to resolve in place or route to the responsible team.

Use dashboards, alarms, and other tools for Networking, AV, and Print services across the global building fleet, interpreting what those signals indicate to solve incidents.

Detect ongoing trends or emerging problems before they occur and define proactive actions to prevent customer impact.

Assess incident scope and severity, correlate related incidents into a single parent incident, and prioritise work against SLAs.

2. Troubleshoot & Support

Resolve issues and support the team's products and systems.

Provide high-quality Tier 1 support for the products and systems in the team's scope, resolving straightforward problems with limited documentation and minimal escalation.

Support critical issues using existing runbooks; maintain composure through difficult interactions until the issue is resolved.

Perform on-call duties on a rotating schedule and respond to emergent events.

Escalate appropriately when resolution requires significant deviation from procedure or when an issue becomes a risk.

3. Subject-Matter Expertise & Technical Leadership

Grow into the go-to person for a focus area.

Develop and apply expertise in one or more focus areas (e.g., Networking, AV, or Print), acting as the technical point of contact for that area within the team.

Give technical direction to others and impart knowledge to users, customers, and teammates.

Lead internal team projects and deliver on defined goals and timelines.

4. Documentation & Operational Improvement

Improve how the team operates.

Identify areas to improve support documentation and processes, and author new runbooks/SOPs and knowledge-base articles where gaps exist.

Identify improvements to existing and new support tools that increase operational efficiency, and help drive their implementation.

Help develop and refine the operational policies and procedures used by the team.

5. Mentoring & Collaboration

Raise the bar for the team.

Serve as a mentor to junior engineers and act as a training buddy for new hires; may assist in hiring activities.

Maintain good working relationships across Amazon and work cross-functionally with partner teams to solve problems and improve processes.

Communicate infrastructure health and trends clearly, both in real time and as inputs to weekly/monthly business reviews.

Basic qualifications

- 1+ years of Windows Server technologies: AD, DFS, Print Services, SCCM experience
- 1+ years of troubleshooting in a multi-user high availability environment experience
- 1+ years of IT client, server, and network service delivery experience
- 1+ years of networking (such as DNS, DHCP, SSL, OSI Model, and TCP/IP) experience
- 1+ years of corporate setting Windows, Mac or Linux Operating systems support experience
- 1+ years of supporting and maintaining a corporate network environment experience
- High school diploma, or equivalent

Preferred qualifications

- 2+ years of computer networking experience, or experience in computer networking
- Experience supporting video conference and teleconference equipment
- Experience that includes strong analytical skills, attention to detail, and effective communication abilities, or experience in Network protocols like DNS/DHCP/TCP

title: Data Engineer, Amazon Security Experience
descriptionHtml:
The Amazon Security Experiences (ASE) organization is the data intelligence backbone of Amazon Security. We build and operate the data platform that powers security insights, builder experience analytics, and tooling decisions across Amazon's security ecosystem. Every insight surfaced to security leadership, from builder productivity trends to security issue quality metrics, flows through systems our team designs, builds, and maintains.

We operate at scale, processing large volumes of security and operational data daily through hundreds of pipelines consisting of transformations, reporting queries, ingestions, and infrastructure management scripts. Our engineers work directly with source systems across AWS and SDO (Security, Developer, and Operations) data domains to procure data, convert it into structured formats, build large-scale processing pipelines, design analytical data models, and maintain infrastructure with the highest security and compliance standards.

We are seeking a Data Engineer I to join our Security Data Intelligence (SDI) team. In this role, you will build and maintain data pipelines that power security analytics across Amazon. Working with well-defined requirements and guidance from senior engineers, you will create physical data models, optimize data pipelines for defined datasets, and deliver reliable, well-documented solutions on schedule. You will partner with teams across ASE, BizOps, MapSec, and other security organizations to implement data ingestion flows and support analytical models that serve the broader Amazon Security organization.

Key job responsibilities
Learn and apply team-established data processing guidelines and best practices when building and testing pipelines. Measure and improve dataset quality across owned pipelines, identifying issues and proposing solutions to the team. Flag limitations or opportunities in data processing tools to senior engineers for evaluation.

Learn and understand the team's existing data architecture, including how security data flows through ingestion, transformation, and serving layers. Build data solutions at the component level within the established team data architecture, following defined logical data models. Create physical data models for assigned datasets, applying appropriate persistence and integration techniques. Understand the implications of implementation decisions (e.g., normalization, distribution) and seek guidance from senior engineers on trade-offs.

Write secure, stable, testable, and maintainable code with minimal defects, following team coding standards. Clearly document solutions for ease of use and maintainability by teammates and data consumers. Get all data models, pipeline designs, and code reviewed by senior engineers before deployment. Test code thoroughly and understand the maintenance characteristics, runtime properties, and dependencies of delivered solutions.

Build and maintain data pipeline infrastructure for assigned datasets using team-established patterns and tools. Apply basic database optimization techniques such as partitioning, distribution, and indexing as directed. Understand the underlying system infrastructure that data solutions depend on, including differences between data persistence solutions. Follow team guidelines for infrastructure management, security compliance, and automation practices.

Solve straightforward, well-defined problems with guidance from senior engineers, for example, building ingestion pipelines for a new security data source where the schema and requirements are defined, or troubleshooting data quality issues in existing datasets by researching root causes and thoroughly resolving defects. Handle problems even outside your own domain by either resolving them or ensuring a clear hand-off to the right owner.

Take well-defined requirements and deliver solutions on schedule within assigned scope. Participate in team design, scoping, and prioritization discussions to understand project context. Manage your own task execution effectively, seeking guidance when blocked or uncertain. Communicate progress and dependencies clearly to your team lead and senior engineers.

Build good working relationships with teammates, peer engineers, and data consumers across ASE and SDO. Partner effectively with Business Analysts, Data Scientists, and peer SDEs to understand data requirements. Help train and mentor DE interns when applicable. Participate in the interview process. Recognize discordant views and participate in constructive dialogue with peers.

Follow team-established best practices for data discovery, naming conventions, and data security. Classify, store, and handle data per Amazon security and compliance policies. Ensure proper access control, data integrity, and auditability for all produced datasets. Track security risks in data handling, mitigate issues, and escalate in a timely manner.

Identify data quality issues and pipeline deficiencies in owned components and propose solutions to the team. Participate in code reviews, design discussions, and team planning sessions. Make small improvements to team development processes when directed. Actively seek knowledge of team data architecture and apply learnings to improve your data solutions.

Participate in on-call rotation and respond to pipeline incidents following established runbooks and escalation procedures. Understand the maintenance characteristics, runtime properties, and dependencies of team data systems. Contribute to monitoring and alarming setup for owned pipelines with guidance from senior engineers. Document incident resolutions and contribute to runbook updates for owned components.

Basic qualifications

- 2+ years of data engineering experience
- Experience with data modeling, warehousing and building ETL pipelines
- Experience with one or more query language (e.g., SQL, PL/SQL, DDL, MDX, HiveQL, SparkSQL, Scala)
- Experience with one or more scripting language (e.g., Python, KornShell)

Preferred qualifications

- Experience with big data technologies such as: Hadoop, Hive, Spark, EMR
- Experience with any ETL tool like, Informatica, ODI, SSIS, BODI, Datastage, etc.

title: Formal Verification Engineer, Annapurna Labs
descriptionHtml:
Annapurna Labs, part of AWS, designs the silicon behind AWS infrastructure, including AWS Graviton processors and the AWS Nitro System. What you prove here runs in millions of servers worldwide.

Formal verification is everywhere in our projects. Each project has hundreds of formal environments, from small blocks with sophisticated data crunching or complex FSMs up to chip-fabric deadlock verification.

The Role:
As an L5 Formal Verification Engineer, you'll own FV for blocks within a Graviton or Nitro subsystem, end to end from architecture to sign-off. You'll work with technical leads and serve as a mentor and knowledge source for other engineers.

Your Ideas Shape the Team:
If a technique works, we adopt it, whoever proposed it. We're pushing AI and agentic flows into everyday verification work, and your ideas will decide how far it goes. Senior engineers on our team are co-inventors on formal verification patents.

What We Offer:
* A role we count on: formal results drive sign-off decisions, and other teams plan around them
* Involvement from day one: FV engineers join at architecture, define what must be proven, and shape designs to be provable before RTL is written
* A real partnership with design: we define verification intent together
* A team where senior FV leaders work alongside early-career engineers who bring energy and fresh ideas. We like the work, and we like working together.

Key job responsibilities
* Own formal verification of your blocks from architecture through sign-off
* Write the formal plan and define what must be proven
* Build formal environments covering FPV, sequential equivalence, connectivity, X-prop, security, and liveness
* Solve convergence problems with abstraction, invariants, and decomposition
* Report clearly what is proven, what is bounded, and what is still open
* Work with design teams to define verification intent and improve design quality
* Bring new techniques, including AI and agentic flows, into team flows

Basic qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering or a related field
- Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field
- 5+ years of hands-on formal verification experience
- Strong knowledge of SystemVerilog Assertions (SVA)
- Hands-on experience with industry formal tools (any vendor)
- Owned formal closure on complex blocks

Preferred qualifications

- Abstraction and complexity-reduction techniques
- Cover-based and semi-formal verification, and helper assertions
- Protocol knowledge: APB, AXI, CHI, networking related
- Experience or strong interest in applying AI to engineering work
- Experience mentoring other engineers

title: Instock Manager , WWGS Inventory Management
descriptionHtml:
Amazon's Worldwide Grocery Stores (WWGS) - Inventory Management business is transforming the grocery shopping experience through innovative retail formats. We are seeking an Instock Manager to join our team and play a critical role in ensuring customers find the products they want, when they want them. This role focuses on managing inventory availability and health across our grocery stores and fulfillment centers, partnering with vendors and internal teams to optimize the customer experience.

Amazon's grocery business has experienced remarkable growth, with groceries becoming some of our most frequently purchased items alongside everyday essentials like paper towels and household products. We've expanded same-day delivery for fresh groceries to over 2,300 U.S. cities, with perishable items like fruits and vegetables leading customer demand.

As an Instock Manager, you will be responsible for tactical execution of inventory strategies, working within defined frameworks to improve in-stock rates and reduce waste. You will analyze data to identify opportunities, manage vendor relationships, and collaborate with cross-functional partners to drive operational improvements. This is an excellent opportunity for someone to build foundational skills in inventory management while making a direct impact on customer satisfaction.

Key job responsibilities
- Manage inventory availability and health metrics to improve in-stock rates and optimize inventory planning.
- Perform business analysis to identify opportunities to improve revenue, profitability, and customer experience.
- Track purchase orders, investigate delivery delays, and resolve order issues with vendors and suppliers.
- Partner with internal teams on purchasing workflows, tools, and process improvements.
- Manage day-to-day operational relationships with vendors and suppliers to ensure consistent product availability.
- Analyze data to identify root causes of inventory issues and implement corrective actions.
- Support forecasting activities by monitoring trends and providing input on demand patterns.
- Collaborate with category teams to understand product assortment and seasonal needs .
- Create reports and dashboards to communicate inventory performance to stakeholders.
- Escalate roadblocks and risks appropriately while learning best practices in supply chain management.

A day in the life
In your day-to-day role, you'll be responsible for the supply chain and inventory management for your assigned categories/sites. You'll continuously deliver results while creating new processes for improvement. You'll analyze data to optimize inventory levels, work with vendors on operational improvements, and partner with internal teams on automation initiatives. You'll also lead cross-functional initiatives that improve customer experience and enable new capabilities for our business, requiring you to pivot based on new challenges and learning.

About the team
The Worldwide Grocery Stores Inventory Management Team is building the future of grocery shopping for our customers, rooted in our innovative supply chain. We are expanding availability of perishable products across our network for both new and existing programs. Our team values problem-solving, analytical thinking, and supply chain understanding. We thrive in a high-energy environment where tactical and strategic activities are driven in parallel, and we're not afraid to roll up our sleeves to deliver results.

descriptionHtml:

Your contributions will be essential in advancing robotics by enabling fluid, reliable, and safe interactions between robots and their environments.

title: Enterprise Customer Success Manager, ASCS - Amazon Freight
descriptionHtml:
Amazon Freight, a key pillar within Amazon Supply Chain Services (ASCS), is looking for a Customer Success Manager to join our Enterprise Account Management team. This is a customer facing relationship management role within our commercial organization. You will serve as the primary operational partner for Amazon Freight's largest enterprise shippers, owning the customer relationship, identifying systemic issues that impact their experience, and coordinating cross functional teams to drive resolution.

Key job responsibilities
• Own the enterprise customer operational relationship across all freight modes (TL, IMDL, LTL), serving as the single threaded point of contact for your accounts' operational points of contact
• Identify systemic operational defects impacting your accounts using performance dashboards and customer feedback. Quantify the problem in dollars, loads, and retention risk
• Coordinate cross functional teams to resolution: gather customer insights, understand requirements, bring the right internal teams together, align on the path forward, and ensure we deliver. You don't solve problems alone but you own making sure they get solved
• Own the customer facing performance narrative. Lead Quarterly Business Reviews, produce recovery plans during performance degradation, and proactively communicate progress on open issues with timelines and measurable targets
• Own escalation communication to customer executives when something goes wrong: what's happening, what we're doing about it, and how we're tracking toward resolution
• Own internal reporting, including MBRs, account bridges, and leading inspection mechanisms for your accounts. Report out on performance metrics, cost inputs, and customer KPIs
• Influence customer operations to drive optimal inputs that lower our costs. Define what good looks like, measure it, and partner with customers to change how they operate
• Activate structured recovery programs before the customer escalates

A day in the life
Your day starts with account health dashboards, spotting a detention-charge trend at one customer's facilities and digging into its cause. By midmorning you're briefing a customer's regional transportation director on performance, then rallying ops and pricing partners on a structural issue hitting multiple facilities. After lunch you build your MBR narrative, quantifying your team's impact and open items. Later you lead a working session with operations and product on a fix to prevent recurring defects, then close by updating a customer VP on a two-week escalation, showing progress against committed targets.

The Enterprise Customer Success team is newly formed within Amazon Freight's commercial organization. descriptionHtml:
Amazon Leo for Government (ALG) is seeking an experienced and highly motivated Operational Program Manager to lead the integration, execution, and delivery of U.S. Government and Department of Defense (DoD) procurement programs for Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellite systems, ground gateways, and ALG uniquely developed products. This role sits at the critical intersection of government sales requirements, supply chain procurement, contract execution, and invoicing ensuring that complex federal acquisition programs move forward with regulatory compliance, operational precision, and accountability.
In this role, you will serve as the central point of coordination between ALG government sales teams (Leo for Government), engineering, supply chain and procurement operations, contracts and compliance, mission assurance, and finance translating unique U.S. Government and DoD satellite communication requirements into executable procurement orders, compliant contract actions, and accurate invoicing workflows. You will be responsible for the detailed analysis and execution of Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) and Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS) requirements, including supply chain risk management provisions under DFARS Part 252.
The ideal candidate thrives in ambiguity, possesses deep knowledge of federal procurement regulations, and has a proven ability to influence and align diverse stakeholders — from engineering and sourcing teams to government contracting officers — without direct authority. You will own the end-to-end operational program lifecycle for government procurement actions, from requirements integration through contract execution, order fulfillment, and financial close-out.


Key job responsibilities
Key Responsibilities
Requirements Integration & Program Strategy
• Integrate and translate requirements from Leo for Government sales teams into actionable procurement plans, ensuring alignment with U.S. Government and DoD contract terms, specifications, and delivery schedules
• Conduct detailed analysis of FAR and DFARS requirements applicable to each procurement action, including but not limited to DFARS Part 252 clauses related to supply chain risk management, cybersecurity (CMMC), counterfeit parts prevention, and Trade Agreements Act (TAA) compliance
• Define program vision, scope, objectives, success criteria, and key milestones for government procurement programs in partnership with ALG leadership, contracts & compliance, and mission assurance teams
• Develop comprehensive procurement execution plans including timelines, resource requirements, supplier dependencies, regulatory compliance checkpoints, and risk assessments

• Coordinate with sourcing leads, engineers, supply chain operations, and third-party suppliers to ensure timely and compliant fulfillment of government orders
• Manage procurement workflows for both commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) items and government-specific configurations requiring anti-tampering, GPS tracking, RFID tagging, secure storage, and supply chain risk management protocols at WAS19
• Oversee Third Party Supplier Assessments (TPSAs) by ensuring engineers and sourcing leads provide required inputs and that assessments meet DFARS supply chain security requirements
• Manage complex interdependencies across procurement actions, engineering milestones, test venue requirements (e.g., Flatsat/HITL), and government delivery schedules

As the critical bridge between Leo engineering teams and procurement execution, this role is the linchpin that builds DoD customer confidence in Leo's mission readiness, ironclad regulatory compliance, and proven ability to put operationally capable Low Earth Orbiting satellite systems, ground gateways, and customer terminals in the warfighter's hands on schedule and within contract terms.

title: Product Designer, AWS Field Experience
descriptionHtml:
AWS Field Experience (AFX) is looking for an innovative UX Designer who wants to help set direction for a strategic AWS initiative supporting a rapidly growing world-wide AWS Sales organization. We are looking for someone who will obsess over delivering the best experience for customers and thrives on the challenge of designing something new that will operate at worldwide scale.

As a successful candidate, you will have a deep understanding of design thinking methodology, and interaction design, designing for and with AI, along with top-notch communications skills. You will take a nimble, creative and pragmatic approach and will possess endless curiosity and passion for delivering customer-focused experiences. As a storyteller, you will influence the business strategy by depicting experiences that demonstrate empathy for users and an innate understanding of their ‘day-to-day’. You will design at pace, balance multiple priorities, and show good judgment when weighing trade-offs. You will be able to distill customer needs from many diverse inputs and provide the clarity needed to solve complex business problems. You will work autonomously, build relationships outside of your immediate team, and demonstrate excellent stakeholder management skills. You will be seen as an expert in your discipline and play a significant role in leading the creative process and advocating for design excellence.



Key job responsibilities
Provide designs for new and existing solutions in consideration of the end-to-end experience from big picture conception to execution. You will be responsible, alongside design leadership, negotiating priorities, achieving alignment on customer problems and product vision. You should be comfortable with designing complex workflows and balancing divergent user perspectives, across a variety of technologies.

Be a self starter and be able to work independently, while actively collaborating and communicating with cross-functional teams, peer designers, management and stakeholders. You will be responsible for building and maintaining healthy and positive relationships with all stakeholders and end users.

Understand the holistic experience and produce designs that integrate seamlessly into our agentic experiences. You will also identify measures that capture the health of the user experience (quantitatively and qualitatively) and actively pursue new opportunities to work backwards from user needs.

Help scale design processes and mechanisms raising the bar on design quality.

A day in the life
Inclusive Team Culture
Here at AWS, we embrace our differences. We are committed to furthering our culture of inclusion. We have ten employee-led affinity groups, reaching 40,000 employees in over 190 chapters globally. We have innovative benefit offerings, and host annual and ongoing learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon (gender diversity) conferences. Amazon’s culture of inclusion is reinforced within our 16 Leadership Principles, which remind team members to seek diverse perspectives, learn and be curious, and earn trust.


Work/Life Balance
Our team puts a high value on work-life balance. It isn’t about how many hours you spend at home or at work; it’s about the flow you establish that brings energy to both parts of your life. We believe striking the right balance between your personal and professional life is critical to life-long happiness and fulfillment. We offer flexibility in working hours and encourage you to find your own balance between your work and personal lives.


Mentorship & Career Growth
Our team is dedicated to supporting new members. We have a broad mix of experience levels and tenures, and we’re building an environment that celebrates knowledge sharing and mentorship. We care about your career growth and strive to assign projects based on what will help each team member develop into a better-rounded professional and enable them to take on more complex tasks in the future.

About the team
Our UX team supports a diverse set of tools and technologies. Our goal is to make sellers effective and efficient in their everyday work, saving them measurable time and effort. As a UX designer on the team, you will be supporting key business initiatives and collaborating with other designers, researchers, program and product managers, developers and senior leaders to develop a comprehensive understanding of our customers and derive meaningful experiences for them. Your work will cover the spectrum of UX design, from exploration and understanding, through planning, design, and execution.

Basic qualifications

title: Site EHS Manager II
descriptionHtml:
Join Amazon’s mission to become Earth’s safest place to work! At Amazon, we’ve set the ambitious goal to become the benchmark of safety excellence across all industries in which we operate. We're seeking a dedicated Workplace Health & Safety (WHS) Manager to join our mission of creating the world's safest work environment. This role offers an exciting opportunity to directly impact associate well being while driving operational excellence.

As a WHS Manager, you'll be the site's safety champion, leading our Global WHS Program implementation. You'll combine hands-on safety management with strategic thinking to protect our most valuable asset – our people. Your role bridges the gap between safety requirements and operational success, requiring both technical expertise and strong interpersonal skills. Working closely with Operations leadership, you'll drive safety initiatives that make a real difference. You'll conduct comprehensive risk assessments, analyze safety data, and implement practical solutions that protect associates while supporting productivity. Your ability to build relationships and influence positive change will be essential as you help shape our safety culture. You'll lead safety compliance efforts, conduct thorough site audits, and analyze incident trends to target improvements where they matter most. Managing our first aid program and emergency response capabilities, you'll ensure immediate care is always available. Your analytical skills will transform safety data into actionable insights, while your leadership abilities will help engage associates in our safety mission.

Core Impact Areas:
Safety Leadership & Innovation - Transform safety culture through leadership and innovative solutions. Drive continuous improvement initiatives that set new benchmarks in workplace safety. Leverage technology and data analytics to drive preventive safety measures that protect our associates while enhancing operational excellence. Develop leadership plans, communicate expectations, and drive initiatives to create a safe work environment. Measure performance against WHS policies, analyze metrics, and conduct site audits to address non-compliance issues.

Strategic Partnership & Influence - Build partnerships with Operations leadership to integrate safety into every aspect of our business. Use compelling data analysis and risk insights to influence positive change and drive strategic decision-making. Establish yourself as a trusted advisor who balances safety excellence with operational demands. Oversee recordkeeping, workplace organization, and WHS training programs.

Additional Job Elements include:
- Lift up to 49 pounds and frequently push, pull, squat, bend, and reach

For those that do not have an adult First Aid, CPR, AED certification from the American Heart Association or American Red Cross, must obtain within 3 weeks of start date.

- Experience implementing lean principles and process improvement in an operational environment.
- Experience in a fast paced, dynamic organization.

- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including comfort interfacing with site leader

title: Paper Packaging Materials Engineer, Global Materials Science
descriptionHtml:
Join Amazon's Global Materials Science (GMS) organization as we pioneer the future of sustainable e-commerce packaging. As an Advanced Materials Engineer based in the EU, you'll serve as the critical link between our European and North American materials science operations, driving materials development tailored to the EU supplier base while harmonizing global materials strategies across regions. Embedded alongside our automation hardware development teams, you'll ensure that packaging materials and automation systems are co-developed for seamless integration.

This is a hands-on, technically broad role spanning pulp and paper manufacturing, packaging converting operations, tape and adhesive systems, coatings, and packaging automation equipment. You'll conduct laboratory research, characterize materials properties, establish specifications, and work directly with EU-based suppliers to bring novel materials from concept to production, while serving as the conduit to align materials globally, simplify where possible, and solve for region-specific requirements driven by regulation, material supply availability, and operational differences.

Key job responsibilities
Materials Development & Innovation:
- Lead laboratory research and development of packaging materials including paper substrates, adhesives, tapes, coatings, and alternative fiber technologies, with deep understanding of pulp and paper manufacturing processes and converting operations.

- Design and execute experiments to optimize material formulations and processing parameters, applying the materials science triangle framework (processing-structure-properties) across the full range of packaging materials and converting processes.

- Develop next-generation materials solutions that unlock step-change improvements in performance, cost, sustainability, and automation compatibility, with specific focus on EU supplier capabilities and regional material availability.

- Advance materials innovations from concept, pilot, and deployment phases, ensuring solutions are compatible with EU packaging automation hardware and converting equipment.

- Evaluate and develop tape, adhesive, and coating systems that meet the unique performance demands of automated packaging lines, considering substrate interactions, machine speed requirements, and environmental conditions.

EU Materials Strategy & Global Alignment:
- Serve as the primary conduit between EU and NA materials science teams, driving global alignment on materials specifications while identifying opportunities to harmonize and simplify across regions.
- Develop and maintain a comprehensive understanding of the EU supplier base, including paper mills, converters, adhesive manufacturers, tape producers, and coating suppliers, and how it differs from the North American supply landscape.
- Identify region-specific materials requirements dictated by EU regulations (e.g., REACH, EU Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation), regional material supply constraints, and operational differences in EU fulfillment networks.
- Balance global standardization with regional customization, driving simplification where materials can be harmonized and developing tailored solutions where regional requirements demand differentiation.
- Build and maintain a materials roadmap for EU that aligns with global GMS strategy and EU automation hardware development timelines.

Automation Hardware Integration:
- Work closely with EU-based automation hardware development teams to ensure packaging materials are co-developed with automation equipment, optimizing for machine runnability, reliability, and throughput.
- Provide materials expertise during automation system design, commissioning, and optimization, translating materials properties into actionable equipment parameters.
- Develop deep understanding of packaging converting equipment (folders, gluers, sealers, tape applicators, labelers) and how materials properties influence machine performance at production speeds.
- Support troubleshooting of materials-related automation failures, conducting root cause analysis that spans materials properties, converting conditions, and equipment settings.

Materials Characterization & Testing:
- Perform and direct lab engineers to conduct comprehensive materials characterization using techniques including tensile/burst/tear testing, rheometry, thermal analysis (DSC, TGA), spectroscopy (FTIR), microscopy (SEM, optical), and surface analysis while utilizing ASTM, TAPPI, ISO, EN, and ISTA standards and non-standard methodologies.
- Establish correlations between fundamental materials properties and operational performance in fulfillment environments, with emphasis on how EU-specific substrates and converting conditions affect outcomes.
- Design and execute test plans that validate materials performance against specifications and requirements for both manual and automated packaging operations.
- Analyze test data using statistical methods to drive data-driven materials selection decisions across the EU supplier base.

Specifications & Quality:
- Define materials specifications based on critical performance thresholds required for packaging to protect products and survive the fulfillment network, accounting for EU-specific substrate variability and supplier capabilities.
- Translate operational requirements and automation equipment constraints into measurable materials properties and acceptable ranges.
- Develop quality control protocols and testing methodologies to ensure EU supplier compliance with specifications, accounting for differences in regional testing standards (EN vs. ASTM/TAPPI).
- Drive specification harmonization between NA and EU where feasible, clearly documenting where and why regional deviations are necessary.

Supplier & Manufacturing Collaboration:
- Work directly with EU-based paper mills, adhesive manufacturers, tape producers, converters, and other suppliers to develop and scale new materials.
- Conduct technical evaluations of EU supplier capabilities, pulp and paper manufacturing processes, converting operations, and quality control systems.
- Guide suppliers on process optimization, from pulp preparation and paper machine settings through converting and finishing operations, to achieve target material properties and consistency.
- Build strong technical relationships across the EU supplier base to enable rapid development cycles and ensure supply resilience.

Cross-Functional Partnership:
- Collaborate with Packaging Design and automation hardware teams on materials-design-equipment integration, ensuring all three dimensions are optimized together.
- Partner with EU and Global Procurement (GPO) on strategic sourcing, supplier selection, and commercial negotiations within the EU supply base.
- Support sustainability initiatives including carbon footprint modeling, recyclability assessment, and compliance with EU-specific sustainability regulations and reporting requirements.
- Provide technical expertise to program managers, product teams, and deployment teams across both EU and NA organizations.
- Communicate complex materials science and manufacturing concepts clearly to technical and non-technical audiences across multiple geographies and cultures.

Documentation & Knowledge Sharing:
- Author technical reports, test protocols, specifications documents, and research summaries that serve both EU and global audiences.
- Document experimental procedures, results, and learnings to build institutional knowledge, with particular emphasis on EU-NA materials differences and lessons learned.
- Present findings at design reviews, technical workshops, and leadership reviews across regions.
- Contribute to intellectual property generation through public disclosures and patent applications.
- Mentor junior engineers and technicians on materials science principles, pulp and paper manufacturing fundamentals, converting operations, and testing methodologies.

A day in the life
You're bridging continents and disciplines—ensuring Amazon's packaging materials work seamlessly from lab bench to automated packaging line.

Your morning starts with a technical review alongside the EU automation hardware team, discussing runnability data from a new paper substrate on their latest packaging machine prototype. The converting parameters need adjustment, your deep knowledge of fiber orientation, surface chemistry, and machine dynamics helps the team identify the right combination of adhesive application weight and compression dwell time.

By midday, you're on a call with a European paper mill, discussing modifications to their pulp furnish and machine settings to improve the tensile energy, a critical property for automated forming operations. You're also comparing their capabilities against what your NA colleagues are achieving with North American suppliers, identifying where specifications can be unified.

Your afternoon shifts to the lab work, where you are directing lab engineer to characterize a new tape system for high-speed application on recycled substrates, and a global alignment session with your NA counterparts. You're presenting a proposal to harmonize adhesive specifications across regions, having identified that three separate specs can be consolidated into one without compromising performance in either geography. Where regulatory or supply differences demand regional solutions, you've clearly documented the rationale and developed parallel qualification paths.

This role sits at the intersection of materials science, manufacturing processes, automation engineering, and global supply chain strategy. Your holistic understanding of how pulp becomes paper, how paper becomes packaging, and how packaging runs through automated systems makes you uniquely positioned to solve problems that span traditional disciplinary boundaries, all while keeping EU and NA aligned on a simplified, high-performing materials portfolio.

About the team
The Global Materials Science (GMS) organization is Amazon's Center of Excellence for packaging materials development and supply chain transformation. Our team represents a fundamental shift in how Amazon approaches packaging innovation, moving from supplier-dependent solutions to owning the invention, development, and optimization of materials that power our fulfillment network.


What Makes Us Unique: We're not just specifying materials. We're fundamentally understanding them through the materials science triangle framework (processing, structure, properties). Our integrated capabilities span from molecular-level materials characterization, to full packaging system testing, to automation compatibility testing. This end-to-end ownership enables us to innovate faster, unlock step-change improvements impossible for suppliers alone, and maintain freedom to operate across multiple supply chains.

Our Impact: We're driving Amazon's transition from plastic to paper packaging, developing breakthrough materials and establishing supply chains that reduce costs while advancing our 2040 net-zero commitment. Our work directly influences automation success, customer experience, and sustainability metrics.

Our Culture: We operate with high technical rigor while moving at startup speed. We embrace calculated risk-taking in R&D, fail fast, and iterate based on data. We believe in radical collaboration, our success requires seamless partnership across engineering, procurement, operations, and sustainability teams. We're building something that's never been done before in e-commerce, and we're looking for engineers who thrive in ambiguity, think globally while executing locally, and are energized by complex, high-impact challenges.

Our Team: We bring together materials scientists, chemists, engineers, and program managers who are passionate about solving hard problems. We partner with world-class academic institutions, leading materials suppliers, and internal Amazon teams to push the boundaries of what's possible in packaging materials. Our EU presence ensures we're co-located with automation development and deeply embedded in the European supplier ecosystem

Basic qualifications

- Experience with the project management of technical projects
- Experience working with interdisciplinary teams to execute product design from concept to production
- Experience in developing functional specifications, design verification plans and functional test procedures
- Experience with materials selection, testing, and scaling to manufacturing
- Bachelor's degree in materials science engineering, chemistry, chemical engineering, mechanical engineering, pulp/paper engineering or a related technical discipline

Preferred qualifications

- Master's degree or higher in materials science engineering, chemistry, chemical engineering, mechanical engineering, pulp/paper engineering or a related technical discipline
- Engineering experience in pulp, paper, packaging or related field.
- Experience in characterization techniques and equipment, such as SEM-EDS, FTIR, DSC, TGA, DMA, rheometry, spectrophotometry, optical microscopy, and mechanical property testing related to packaging or other forest products with standard (ASTM, TAPPI, ISO, ISTA, etc.) and non standard methodologies.

title: Network Development Engineer, 5G NTN Network Integration and Test, Amazon Leo
descriptionHtml:
Amazon Leo is building a Low Earth Orbit satellite constellation to deliver high speed, low latency broadband connectivity to unserved and underserved communities around the world. As part of Payload Integration and Test, this role is focused on hands on integration, validation, troubleshooting, and qualification of end to end satellite communications systems across space, ground, RF, modem, RAN, Core, transport, and cloud infrastructure. The work is lab centered and system focused. The role is not a software development position, but the ability to use Linux, Python, protocol traces, packet captures, and automation to debug complex systems is highly valuable.

Export Control Requirement
Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident that is a current Green Card holder, or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.


Key job responsibilities
This role owns the network integration path between Open RAN, 5G Core, IMS, transport, lab infrastructure, and satellite payload test systems. The candidate should be able to debug across CU, DU, RU, gNodeB, Core, routing, switching, tunnels, packet captures, and lab hardware without needing the problem to be pre isolated by another team.

Key Job Responsibilities
• Integrate and validate end to end network connectivity across Open RAN, gNodeB, 5G Core, IMS, transport, and LEO satellite test systems.
• Validate 3GPP Release 17 NTN behaviors from a network integration perspective, including attach, registration, bearer setup, user plane, mobility, and service continuity.
• Integrate and test Open RAN architecture components including CU, DU, RU, F1, E1, Xn, and gNodeB connectivity into lab and payload environments.
• Validate VoNR and IMS call flows, including registration, SIP signaling, media path, QoS, emergency call behavior where applicable, and failure recovery.
• Troubleshoot NGC, NGU, NGAP, GTP U, SCTP, PFCP, VLANs, routing, MPLS, Segment Routing, QoS, MTU, timing, and user plane performance issues.
• Build and execute integration, regression, interoperability, failover, resiliency, and performance test plans for lab and HIL environments.
• Use packet captures, protocol logs, Linux tools, telemetry, and system traces to drive root cause across RF, RAN, Core, payload, transport, and cloud teams.
• Partner with RF, modem, payload, Core, RAN, software, and systems teams to define pass fail criteria and drive issues from ambiguous system behavior to clear resolver ownership.
• Support readiness reviews, test reports, and operational handoff for production bound satellite terrestrial network capabilities.

Basic qualifications

- Associate's degree or above
- 5+ years experience integrating, testing, or operating LTE or 5G networks in lab, carrier, vendor, or large scale production environments.
- Strong practical knowledge of 3GPP network architecture, including RAN to Core interfaces and 5G user plane and control plane flows.
- Experience with Open RAN or disaggregated RAN architecture, including CU, DU, RU, gNodeB integration, and related interfaces.
- Knowledge of 3GPP Release 17 NTN concepts and ability to apply standards knowledge during integration and troubleshooting.
- Experience with VoNR and IMS protocols, including SIP, RTP, registration, call setup, media path validation, and failure analysis.
- Strong Linux networking skills and ability to troubleshoot routing, interfaces, packet captures, firewalls, tunnels, timing, and performance.
- Experience with Wireshark or equivalent tools for packet and protocol analysis.
- Experience working in hands on lab environments with physical infrastructure, HIL setups, network equipment, and multi team debug.

Preferred qualifications

- Experience with LEO, satellite communications, NTN, or space to ground network integration.
- Experience with 3GPP Release 18 NTN or emerging NTN standards.
- Experience with MOCN, MORAN, Multi PLMN broadcast, PLMN operations, network slicing, or shared RAN deployments.
- Experience with Cisco, Juniper, Arista, MikroTik, or comparable routing and switching platforms.
- Experience with MPLS, Segment Routing, EVPN, VXLAN, BGP, OSPF, IS IS, QoS, and high availability transport design.
- Python scripting experience for test automation, log parsing, packet analysis, or lab tooling.
- Experience with Kubernetes, cloud networking, CI based regression, or automated lab orchestration.
- Experience producing clear test reports, defect summaries, and executive ready readiness assessments.
